rodulf-king-of-the-heruli.s: Rodulf was king of the Heruli on the middle Danube in the early 6th century. Around 507 the Ostrogothic king Theodoric the Great adopted him as his son in arms, binding him to the Ostrogothic alliance.

rushen-abbey.s: Rushen Abbey was a monastery at Ballasalla in the south of the Isle of Man, founded in 1134 by King Olaf I of Mann and the Isles and later part of the Cistercian order. It was the island's most important religious house, and the Chronicle of the Kings of Mann and the Isles is…

river-nene.s: The River Nene rises in Northamptonshire in the English Midlands and flows north-east through Northampton, Peterborough and Wisbech to the Wash. Its valley was a corridor of settlement from prehistoric times, home to the Middle Angles in the early Middle Ages and to the abbey…

river-welland.s: The River Welland rises in Northamptonshire in the English Midlands and flows north-east past Market Harborough, Stamford and Spalding to the Wash. For much of its course it forms county boundaries, and its valley was one of the early homelands of the Middle Angles.

regni.s: The Regni or Regnenses were the people of the Roman civitas centred on Noviomagus Reginorum, modern Chichester, in what is now Sussex. The area formed part of the client kingdom of Togidubnus after the Roman conquest of 43.

rechiar.s: Rechiar was king of the Suebi from 448 to 456, the first Germanic king known to have been a Catholic and the first to mint coins in his own name. He married a daughter of the Visigothic king Theodoric I and raided widely in Hispania.

rimbert.s: Rimbert was archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen from 865 to 888 and the disciple and successor of Ansgar. His Life of Ansgar is the most important written source for Sweden in the 9th century, describing Birka, its kings and Ansgar's missions there.

republic-of-the-congo.s: The Republic of the Congo is a country in Central Africa on the north bank of the Congo River, with Brazzaville as its capital. As the French colony of Middle Congo it was part of French Equatorial Africa, and it became independent on 15 August 1960.

rukidi-iv-of-toro.s: Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV is omukama, or king, of Toro in western Uganda. He succeeded his father, Patrick Kaboyo Olimi VII, in 1995 at the age of three, two years after Uganda restored its traditional kingdoms, and ruled under regents until he came of age.

rwenzori-mountains.s: The Rwenzori Mountains are a range on the border between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rising to 5,109 metres at Margherita Peak on Mount Stanley. They carry some of Africa's last equatorial glaciers and are often identified with Ptolemy's Mountains of the…

rusa-i.s: Rusa I was king of Urartu in the later 8th century BCE, ruling from about 735 to 714 BCE. He faced attacks from the Cimmerians in the north and the Assyrian Empire in the south.

revolt-of-the-brotherhoods.s: The Revolt of the Brotherhoods, or Germanies, was a rising of the craft guilds of Valencia and other towns of the kingdom against the nobility between 1519 and 1523. Armed brotherhoods formed to defend the coast took control of the city and fought the nobles and their Muslim…

ragnall-ua-imair.s: Ragnall ua Ímair was a Viking leader, a grandson of Ímar, the founder of the Uí Ímair dynasty of Dublin. In 914 his fleet established a base at Waterford, from which he raided Munster.

raymond-fitzgerald.s: Raymond FitzGerald, called le Gros, was a Cambro-Norman knight who took part in the English invasion of Ireland. Sent ahead by Strongbow in 1170, he landed at Baginbun and defeated a force from Waterford, and he joined Strongbow in storming the town that August.

reginalds-tower.s: Reginald's Tower is a round stone tower on the quay of Waterford, Ireland, at the apex of the old walled town. Tradition links it to a Viking fortification of the 10th or 11th century, though the present building is mainly Anglo-Norman work of the 12th and 13th centuries.

robert-bosch.s: Robert Bosch was a German engineer and industrialist from Württemberg. He opened a workshop for precision mechanics and electrical engineering in Stuttgart in 1886 and made his fortune with magneto ignition systems for motor engines.

rai-people.s: The Rai are a group of Tibeto-Burman-speaking Kiranti peoples of the hills of eastern Nepal, with communities in Sikkim and Darjeeling. They speak more than twenty related languages, among them Bantawa, Chamling and Kulung.

raghudev-narayan.s: Raghudev Narayan was the son of the Koch general Chilarai and the first ruler of Koch Hajo, the eastern part of the Koch kingdom in present-day Assam. In 1581 his uncle Nara Narayan gave him the lands east of the Sankosh river.

ramagrama.s: Ramagrama was the main town of the Koliyas, a clan republic of the Buddha's time in the foothills of present-day Nepal. Buddhist texts say the Koliyas received a share of the Buddha's relics and built a stupa there, which according to legend was the only original relic stupa…

ratan-singh-of-bundi.s: Ratan Singh was Rao of Bundi, a Hada Chauhan Rajput state in Rajasthan, from 1607 to 1631, and a commander in the service of the Mughal emperors. He fought for them in the Deccan and was rewarded with high rank.

rurik.s: Rurik was a Varangian chieftain who, according to the Primary Chronicle, was invited in 862 by Slavic and Finnic tribes of the north to rule them, settling at Ladoga and then Novgorod. He was regarded as the founder of the Rurikid dynasty, which ruled Kievan Rus' and later…

rigveda.s: The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas, the sacred texts of Hinduism: a collection of 1,028 Sanskrit hymns arranged in ten books. Composed in north-western India roughly between 1500 and 1000 BCE and handed down orally with great precision, it praises gods such as Indra,…

rajasuya.s: The Rajasuya was a Vedic royal consecration ritual in which a king was anointed and proclaimed his supremacy over other rulers. Described in the Yajurveda and the Brahmanas, it involved a long series of ceremonies, including a mock cattle raid and a game of dice.

russian-far-east.s: The Russian Far East is the easternmost part of Russia, between eastern Siberia and the Pacific Ocean, including the Amur and Primorye regions, Kamchatka, Sakhalin and Chukotka. Russia acquired its southern parts from Qing China by the treaties of Aigun in 1858 and Peking in…

riad-al-solh.s: Riad Al Solh was a Lebanese nationalist politician and the first prime minister of independent Lebanon. A Sunni Muslim from Sidon, he made the National Pact of 1943 with President Bechara El Khoury and led the struggle that ended the French mandate.

rusyns.s: The Rusyns are an East Slavic people of the Carpathian mountains, living mainly in Transcarpathian Ukraine, eastern Slovakia and south-eastern Poland, with a large diaspora in North America. Most belong to the Greek Catholic or Orthodox churches.

rasa-river.s: The Raša is a short river in eastern Istria, Croatia, flowing into the Bay of Raša on the Kvarner Gulf. In antiquity, as the Arsia, it marked the boundary between the Histri and the Liburnians, and from the time of Augustus it formed the eastern limit of Italy's tenth region,…

rimac-river.s: The Rímac is a river of Peru's central coast that flows from the Andes through the centre of Lima to the Pacific at Callao. Its valley held the Maranga complex of the Lima culture and later shrines of the Ychsma, and Francisco Pizarro founded Lima on its south bank in 1535.

roland-lord-of-galloway.s: Roland (Lochlann) was lord of Galloway from 1185 to 1200, a grandson of Fergus of Galloway. After his father Uhtred was murdered by his uncle Gilla Brigte, he reunited Galloway on Gilla Brigte's death, with the acceptance of Henry II of England.

rocca-di-ravaldino.s: The Rocca di Ravaldino is a fortress in Forlì in Romagna, rebuilt in the later 15th century. It is famous for Caterina Sforza's defiance there in 1488 after the murder of her husband Girolamo Riario, which saved the lordship for her son.

rustringen.s: Rüstringen was a medieval Frisian land around the Jade bay in north-western Germany, before storm floods enlarged the bay. Its free peasant communities kept their own law code, the Rüstringen law, among the oldest texts in Old Frisian.

rudnik.s: Rudnik is a mountain in central Serbia, south of Belgrade, whose name means 'mine'. Its silver and lead mines, worked from the 13th century with the help of Saxon miners, were among the richest in medieval Serbia.

raynald-of-chatillon.s: Raynald of Châtillon was a French knight who became Prince of Antioch by marriage in 1153 and, after years as a captive in Aleppo, Lord of Oultrejordain through his marriage to Stephanie of Milly in 1176. From Kerak he raided Muslim caravans and in 1182–1183 sent ships into…

reggia-carrarese.s: The Reggia Carrarese was the palace of the Carrara lords of Padua, built in the 14th century in the centre of the city. Its richly decorated halls made it one of the grandest princely residences of its time in Italy.

rocca-costanza.s: Rocca Costanza is a Renaissance fortress in Pesaro, on the Adriatic coast of Italy. It was begun in 1474 by Costanzo I Sforza, lord of Pesaro, to designs by Luciano Laurana, and completed under his son Giovanni Sforza.

reuss-river.s: The Reuss is a river in central Switzerland, about 160 kilometres long. Rising near the Gotthard Pass, it flows through the canton of Uri and the Schöllenen gorge into Lake Lucerne, leaves the lake at the city of Lucerne and joins the Aare near Brugg.

roccagloriosa.s: Roccagloriosa is a village in the southern Cilento, Campania, near which lies a fortified Lucanian settlement of the 4th century BCE. Excavations there have revealed defensive walls, houses and rich tombs, making it one of the best-studied Lucanian hill towns and an important…

rossano-di-vaglio.s: Rossano di Vaglio is an archaeological site near Vaglio Basilicata, north-east of Potenza in southern Italy. It was the federal sanctuary of the Lucanians, dedicated to the goddess Mefitis, used from the 4th century BCE into the Roman period.

rechila.s: Rechila was king of the Suebi in Gallaecia from 438 to 448. After the Vandals left Hispania for Africa, he campaigned south, defeating a Roman force on the Genil, taking Emerita Augusta in 439 and Seville in 441, so that Suebic power extended over much of Lusitania, Baetica…

redarii.s: The Redarii were a West Slavic tribe of the Lutician federation, living around the Tollensesee and Lake Lieps in modern Mecklenburg, Germany. Their territory held Rethra, the federation's chief temple, which gave them leading influence among the Lutici.

radegast.s: Radegast is a name linked with Rethra, the chief sanctuary of the West Slavic Lutici. Thietmar of Merseburg, writing around 1015, called the place Riedegost and its main god Zuarasici (Svarožič), while Adam of Bremen in the 1070s named the god himself Radegast.

rethra.s: Rethra was the chief temple-fortress of the Lutici, a West Slavic federation between the Elbe and the Oder, in the land of the Redarii. Thietmar of Merseburg and Adam of Bremen describe its wooden temple, idols and an oracle using a sacred horse.

revival-le-dynasty.s: The Revival Lê dynasty was the restored Lê imperial line of Vietnam from 1533 to 1789. After the Mạc seized the throne in 1527, loyalists under Nguyễn Kim set up a Lê emperor in Thanh Hóa, and this southern court fought the Mạc until it retook Thăng Long in 1592.

richard-an-iarainn-bourke.s: Richard an Iarainn Bourke, called 'Iron Dick', was a Gaelicised Burke lord of Mayo who became The Mac William Íochtar in 1580. He was the second husband of the sea captain Grace O'Malley, and their son was Tibbot na Long Bourke.

rani-mangammal.s: Rani Mangammal was queen regent of the Madurai Nayak kingdom from about 1689 to 1704, on behalf of her grandson Vijaya Ranga Chokkanatha. She kept the kingdom intact through diplomacy with the Mughals and campaigns against Thanjavur and Travancore.

roberto-de-nobili.s: Roberto de Nobili was an Italian Jesuit missionary who worked at Madurai from 1606. He adopted the dress, diet and customs of a Hindu sannyasi, learned Tamil and Sanskrit, and presented Christianity in Indian terms to win converts from the high castes.

ravi-shankar.s: Ravi Shankar was an Indian sitar virtuoso and composer who trained under Allauddin Khan at Maihar. From the 1950s he brought Hindustani classical music to Western audiences through tours, recordings and his work with the Beatles' George Harrison and the violinist Yehudi Menuhin.

richard-ii-of-england.s: Richard II was King of England from 1377 to 1399, succeeding his grandfather Edward III at the age of ten. As a boy of fourteen he faced the rebels of the Peasants' Revolt in 1381.

reign-of-terror.s: The Reign of Terror was the period of the French Revolution, from September 1793 to July 1794, in which the revolutionary government used mass arrests and executions against those it considered enemies of the Revolution. Directed by the Committee of Public Safety, in which…

reconstruction-era.s: The Reconstruction era was the period after the American Civil War, from 1865 to 1877, in which the United States reintegrated the defeated Southern states and tried to secure the rights of some four million freed people. The Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments…

ramakrishna-mission.s: The Ramakrishna Mission is a Hindu religious and philanthropic organisation founded in 1897 by Swami Vivekananda and named after his teacher, the Bengali mystic Ramakrishna. Combining monastic life with social service, it runs schools, hospitals and relief work in India and…

revolutions-of-1989.s: The revolutions of 1989 were the wave of largely peaceful uprisings that overthrew the communist regimes of Central and Eastern Europe. Beginning with negotiated change in Poland, where the trade union Solidarity won partly free elections in June, they spread to Hungary, East…

rastatt-palace.s: Rastatt Palace is a Baroque residence in Rastatt, Baden-Württemberg, built from 1700 for Margrave Louis William of Baden-Baden after French troops burned Baden-Baden in 1689. Modelled on Versailles, it was the first Baroque palace of its kind on the Upper Rhine.

rotteln-castle.s: Rötteln Castle is a large castle ruin above Lörrach in south-western Baden-Württemberg. It passed in 1315 to the margraves of Hachberg-Sausenberg, who made it their residence, and later to the margraves of Baden.

rhone.s: The Rhône is a major river of Switzerland and France, about 810 kilometres long. It rises in the Rhône Glacier in the Swiss Alps, flows through Lake Geneva and Lyon, and reaches the Mediterranean in a wide delta in the Camargue.

rajasthan.s: Rajasthan is the largest state of India by area, in the north-west of the country on the border with Pakistan. It includes the Thar Desert west of the Aravalli Range and more fertile land to the south-east.

rajyashri.s: Rajyashri was an Indian princess of the Pushyabhuti dynasty of Thanesar, daughter of Prabhakaravardhana and sister of Rajyavardhana and Harsha. Married to the Maukhari king Grahavarman of Kannauj, she was imprisoned after he was killed around 606 but escaped; according to…

radama-i.s: Radama I was king of the Merina kingdom of Madagascar from 1810 to 1828, son of Andrianampoinimerina. Allied with Britain from 1817, he received arms and advisers, built a standing army and conquered much of the island, taking the title king of Madagascar.

rainilaiarivony.s: Rainilaiarivony was prime minister of the Merina kingdom of Madagascar from 1864 to 1895 and its real ruler. He married three successive queens, Rasoherina, Ranavalona II and Ranavalona III, brought the court to Protestant Christianity and modernised the law, schools and army.

ranavalona-i.s: Ranavalona I was queen of the Merina kingdom of Madagascar from 1828 to 1861, widow of Radama I. She resisted European influence, expelled missionaries, persecuted Malagasy Christians and kept up conscription and wars of conquest, and in 1845 her forces repelled a joint…

ranavalona-ii.s: Ranavalona II was queen of the Merina kingdom of Madagascar from 1868 to 1883. Married to the prime minister Rainilaiarivony, who held real power, she was baptised a Protestant in 1869, after which the royal idols were burned and Christianity spread rapidly among the Merina.

rova-of-antananarivo.s: The Rova of Antananarivo is the royal palace complex of the Merina kingdom on the highest hill of Antananarivo, Madagascar. It held the palaces and tombs of the Merina rulers from the seventeenth century, including the great Manjakamiadana palace, built of wood and later…

rudiae.s: Rudiae was a Messapian town in the Salento peninsula of southern Italy, near present-day Lecce. Its walls and tombs date back to at least the sixth century BCE, and it later became a Roman municipium.

republic-of-serbian-krajina.s: The Republic of Serbian Krajina was a self-proclaimed Serb state in Croatia, declared in 1991 by Croatian Serbs opposed to Croatian independence and backed by the Yugoslav army and Serbia. It covered about a third of Croatia, including the old Military Frontier lands, with its…

romanos-iii-argyros.s: Romanos III Argyros was Byzantine emperor from 1028 to 1034, a senior aristocrat who came to the throne by marrying Zoe, daughter of Constantine VIII. In 1030 he led an army against the Mirdasid emirate of Aleppo and was heavily defeated near Azaz, though his general George…

ravanica.s: Ravanica is a Serbian Orthodox monastery in central Serbia, founded in the 1370s by Prince Lazar as his burial church. Its church, with five domes and richly decorated façades, is the earliest major work of the Morava school of architecture.

rigoberto-cabezas.s: Rigoberto Cabezas was a Nicaraguan journalist, soldier and politician. In 1894 President José Santos Zelaya sent him to the Caribbean coast, where he occupied Bluefields and oversaw the incorporation of the Mosquito Reserve into Nicaragua as the department of Zelaya.

rattlesnake-disk.s: The Rattlesnake Disk is a round sandstone palette found at Moundville in Alabama in 1883. Engraved with an open hand bearing an eye, encircled by two knotted horned rattlesnakes, it is one of the best-known objects of the Mississippian culture's religious art.

reglement-organique-mount-lebanon.s: The Règlement Organique was the statute agreed in 1861 between the Ottoman government and Britain, France, Austria, Prussia and Russia after the civil war of 1860 in Mount Lebanon. It made the mountain a single autonomous district, the Mutasarrifate, governed by a non-Lebanese…

rohingya.s: The Rohingya are a mainly Muslim people of Rakhine State in western Myanmar, close to the border with Bangladesh. Myanmar's 1982 citizenship law left most of them stateless, and they have faced repeated persecution.

rabbel-ii.s: Rabbel II was the last king of the Nabataeans, reigning from about 70 to 106 CE. He came to the throne as a boy under his mother's regency and appears to have favoured Bostra in the north of the kingdom.

ripudaman-singh.s: Ripudaman Singh was Maharaja of Nabha, a Sikh princely state in the Punjab, from 1911 to 1923. He supported Sikh religious reform and Indian nationalist causes, which brought him into conflict with the British.

romowe.s: Romowe was a sacred site of the pagan Prussians described in the chronicle of Peter of Dusburg of 1326, which places it in Nadruvia and calls it the seat of a high priest, the Kriwe, revered like a pope. No archaeological trace has been found, and many historians doubt that it…

rakaposhi.s: Rakaposhi is a mountain of the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, rising to 7,788 metres above the Nagar valley. It is noted for one of the greatest uninterrupted rises from base to summit in the world.

rudrasena-i.s: Rudrasena I was a king of the Vakataka dynasty in central India in the 4th century, the grandson and successor of Pravarasena I. His mother was a daughter of Bhava Naga, king of the Bharashiva Nagas, and the alliance with the Naga house strengthened his position.

raghuji-iii-bhonsle.s: Raghuji III Bhonsle was the last Maratha raja of Nagpur, placed on the throne as a boy in 1818 after the deposition of Appa Sahib and kept under close British supervision during his minority. When he died in 1853 without a son or adopted heir, Governor-General Lord Dalhousie…

russo-persian-war-1826-1828.s: The Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828 began when Qajar Iran, led by Crown Prince Abbas Mirza, attacked Russian-held territory in the South Caucasus to recover lands lost in 1813. After early successes the Persians were defeated at Ganja, and the Russians under Ivan Paskevich took…

ranjitsinhji.s: Ranjitsinhji was an Indian prince and cricketer who played for Sussex and in Test matches for England from 1896 to 1902, and became one of the most celebrated batsmen of his age. In 1907 he became Jam Sahib, ruler of the princely state of Nawanagar in Gujarat, where he…

roossenekal.s: Roossenekal is a small town in Mpumalanga, South Africa, north-east of Middelburg. It was founded after the Mapoch War of 1882–1883 near the former Ndzundza Ndebele stronghold of KwaMaza and named after Roos and Senekal, two Boer officers killed in that war.

ragenfrid.s: Ragenfrid was mayor of the palace of Neustria from 715, chosen by the Neustrian nobles to lead them against the Austrasian family of Pippin of Herstal. Allied with the Frisian king Radbod, he fought Charles Martel, who defeated him at Amblève in 716, at Vinchy in 717 and near…

recollects.s: The Recollects were a reformed branch of the Franciscan order that took shape in France in the late 16th century. In 1615 four Recollect friars arrived in New France at Samuel de Champlain's invitation, becoming the colony's first missionaries, and worked among the Huron and…

rensselaerswyck.s: Rensselaerswyck was the most successful patroonship of New Netherland, a vast estate around Fort Orange on both banks of the upper Hudson River, founded in 1630 by the Amsterdam merchant Kiliaen van Rensselaer. Tenants farmed its land and traded furs under the patroon's…

real-plan.s: The Real Plan, or Plano Real, was the economic stabilisation programme that ended chronic hyperinflation in Brazil in 1994. Prepared under finance minister Fernando Henrique Cardoso, it introduced a transitional unit of account, the URV, and then a new currency, the real,…

ruvuma-river.s: The Ruvuma, called the Rovuma in Portuguese, is a river of East Africa, about 800 km long, that rises in southern Tanzania and flows east to the Indian Ocean. For most of its course it forms the border between Tanzania and Mozambique, agreed between Germany and Portugal in 1886.

rivas-nicaragua.s: Rivas is a city in south-western Nicaragua, capital of the Rivas department, on the narrow isthmus between Lake Nicaragua and the Pacific Ocean. The area was home to the Nahua-speaking Nicarao, whose ruler met the Spanish conquistador Gil González Dávila in 1523.

rajuvula.s: Rajuvula was an Indo-Scythian ruler, styled great satrap, who governed Mathura in northern India around the turn of the 1st century BCE and the 1st century CE. He issued coins copying those of the Indo-Greek kings.

rhins-of-galloway.s: The Rhins of Galloway is a hammer-headed peninsula in the far south-west of Scotland, joined to the mainland by a narrow isthmus between Loch Ryan and Luce Bay. Its southern tip, the Mull of Galloway, is Scotland's most southerly point, and Stranraer and Portpatrick lie on it.

raramuri.s: The Rarámuri, or Tarahumara, are an Indigenous people of the Sierra Madre Occidental in the Mexican state of Chihuahua, speaking a Uto-Aztecan language. Jesuit missions reached them in the early 17th century, and they rose in several revolts in the mid- and late 17th century…

reynosa.s: Reynosa is a city in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas, on the south bank of the Rio Grande opposite McAllen, Texas. It was founded in 1749 by José de Escandón as one of the first settlements of the colony of Nuevo Santander.

raqqa.s: Raqqa is a city on the north bank of the Euphrates in northern Syria. Known in Hellenistic and Roman times as Nikephorion and Kallinikos, it was the residence of the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid from 796 to 808, and in the 10th and 11th centuries it was held in turn by the…

reric.s: Reric was an early medieval trading port of the Obotrites on the Baltic coast, usually identified with the excavated site at Groß Strömkendorf on Wismar Bay in Mecklenburg. Frankish annals record that the Danish king Gudfred destroyed it in 808 and moved its merchants to Hedeby.

rhoemetalces-iii.s: Rhoemetalces III was the last king of Thrace, a Roman client ruler of the Sapaean house. The emperor Caligula made him king of Thrace in 38 CE, at a time when Rome governed the region through native princes.

rogozen-treasure.s: The Rogozen Treasure is a hoard of 165 Thracian silver vessels, many partly gilded, found in 1985–1986 near the village of Rogozen in north-western Bulgaria. Dating mainly from the 5th and 4th centuries BCE, it includes phialai, jugs and cups, several inscribed with the names…

raj-darbhanga.s: Raj Darbhanga was a great landholding estate in the Mithila region of northern Bihar, India, held by the Khandavala family of Maithil Brahmins. Recognised by the Mughals in the 16th century and confirmed by the British, it became one of the largest zamindari estates in British…

ram-raja-temple.s: The Ram Raja Temple is a Hindu temple in Orchha, Madhya Pradesh, where the god Rama is worshipped as a reigning king. According to tradition, Queen Ganesh Kunwari of Orchha brought an image of Rama from Ayodhya in the 16th century, and it could not be moved from the palace…

ram-singh-i.s: Ram Singh I was the Kachhwaha Rajput ruler of Amber from 1667 to 1688 and a general of the Mughal Empire. Aurangzeb sent him to reconquer the lower Brahmaputra valley from the Ahom kingdom, and in 1671 his army and fleet were defeated by Lachit Borphukan at the Battle of…

rang-ghar.s: The Rang Ghar is a two-storeyed brick pavilion at Rangpur, near Sivasagar in Assam, built around 1746 under the Ahom king Pramatta Singha. It served as a royal stand from which kings and nobles watched buffalo fights and other games during the Rongali Bihu festival, and its…

rangpur-assam.s: Rangpur was a capital of the Ahom kingdom, on the outskirts of present-day Sivasagar in Assam, India, not to be confused with Rangpur in Bangladesh. Founded by Rudra Singha in the early eighteenth century, it was the main royal seat for much of that century, when kings built…

rudra-singha.s: Rudra Singha, or Sukhrungphaa, was king of the Ahom kingdom of Assam from 1696 to 1714, under whom the state reached the height of its power. Succeeding his father Gadadhar Singha, he brought the Kachari and Jaintia kingdoms under Ahom influence, founded Rangpur and patronised…

respendial.s: Respendial was a king of the Alans who led one of their groups across the Rhine into Gaul with the Vandals and Suebi, traditionally on 31 December 406. According to Gregory of Tours, drawing on the lost history of Renatus Profuturus Frigeridus, his Alans saved the Vandals from…

rando.s: Rando was an Alemannic prince who in 368 surprised the Roman city of Mainz while its garrison was absent and its people were celebrating a Christian festival, carrying off many captives and much plunder. The raid provoked Valentinian I's invasion of Alemannic territory that…

reverter-de-la-guardia.s: Reverter de La Guardia was a Catalan nobleman who commanded the Christian mercenary troops serving the Almoravid emirs in Morocco in the 1130s and 1140s. Known in Arabic sources as al-Ruburtayr, he led Almoravid forces against the rising Almohads and was killed fighting them…

revolucion-libertadora.s: The Revolución Libertadora, or Liberating Revolution, was the military coup of September 1955 that overthrew Juan Perón and the military government that followed until 1958, led first by Eduardo Lonardi and then by Pedro Eugenio Aramburu. It banned Peronism, repressed a…

revolution-of-the-park.s: The Revolution of the Park was an armed uprising in Buenos Aires in July 1890 by the Civic Union, led by Leandro Alem, against President Miguel Juárez Celman, named after the artillery park where the rebels gathered. It was defeated within days, but it forced Juárez Celman to…

riccheri-law.s: The Riccheri Law was the Argentine law of 1901 that introduced compulsory military service for young men, named after the minister of war, Pablo Riccheri. Passed during a naval and military rivalry with Chile, it created a conscript army and was also meant to integrate the…

roca-runciman-treaty.s: The Roca–Runciman Treaty was a trade agreement signed in 1933 by Argentine Vice-President Julio Argentino Roca Jr and the British trade minister Walter Runciman. Britain guaranteed a quota for Argentine chilled beef, while Argentina made concessions to British companies and…

royal-hungarian-honved.s: The Royal Hungarian Honvéd was the territorial army of the Kingdom of Hungary within Austria-Hungary, created in 1868 after the Compromise of 1867, with Hungarian as its language of command. Its name recalled the Hungarian revolutionary army of 1848–1849.

raba.s: The Rába, in German Raab, is a river of Central Europe that rises in Styria in Austria and flows north-east through western Hungary to join a branch of the Danube at Győr. In 791 Charlemagne's campaign against the Avars advanced as far as the Rába, and in 1664 the Battle of…

richard-harliston.s: Sir Richard Harliston was an English naval commander and Yorkist supporter who recovered Jersey for Edward IV. In 1468, with English ships and the help of islanders, he besieged Mont Orgueil, which had been held by the French since 1461, and forced its surrender.

robert-blake.s: Robert Blake was an English admiral who commanded the navy of the Commonwealth. A Parliamentarian officer in the English Civil War, he became a general at sea in 1649, destroyed Prince Rupert's royalist fleet, took Jersey and the Scilly Isles in 1651 and fought the Dutch in…

rajmahal.s: Rajmahal is a town on the Ganges in the Sahibganj district of Jharkhand, India, at the gateway between Bihar and Bengal. In 1576 the Mughals defeated the last Bengal sultan near it.

richard-eaton.s: Richard M. Eaton is an American historian of South Asia, long a professor at the University of Arizona.

rukunuddin-barbak-shah.s: Rukunuddin Barbak Shah was sultan of Bengal from 1459 to 1474, of the Ilyas Shahi dynasty and son of Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah. He extended the kingdom by campaigns in the south and east, and was a patron of Persian and Bengali learning, among them the poet Maladhar Basu.

rupa-goswami.s: Rupa Goswami was a theologian and poet of Gaudiya Vaishnavism, one of the six Goswamis of Vrindavan. With his brother Sanatana he served Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah of Bengal as a high official before leaving to follow Chaitanya, who sent him to Vrindavan.

republican-manifesto.s: The Republican Manifesto was a declaration published in Rio de Janeiro on 3 December 1870 in the first issue of the newspaper A República, launching an organised republican movement in the Brazilian Empire. Drafted largely by the journalist Quintino Bocaiúva and signed by…

reginald-dyer.s: Reginald Dyer was a British Indian Army officer who ordered the Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar on 13 April 1919. Without warning, his troops fired on an unarmed crowd gathered in an enclosed garden, killing at least 379 people by official figures and probably many more.

radcliffe-line.s: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary drawn in 1947 between India and Pakistan in Punjab and Bengal, named after the British lawyer Sir Cyril Radcliffe, who chaired the two boundary commissions. Radcliffe had never been to India and had about five weeks for the task.

round-table-conferences-india.s: The Round Table Conferences were three meetings held in London between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reform in British India. They brought together British politicians, Indian princes and representatives of Indian parties and communities.

rowlatt-act.s: The Rowlatt Act was a law passed by the Imperial Legislative Council of British India in March 1919, extending wartime emergency powers. Based on the report of a committee chaired by the judge Sidney Rowlatt, it allowed the detention of suspected revolutionaries without trial…

royal-titles-act-1876.s: The Royal Titles Act 1876 was a law of the British Parliament that allowed Queen Victoria to take the title Empress of India. Promoted by the prime minister Benjamin Disraeli, it was opposed by many Liberals as un-English.

red-river-expedition-1870.s: The Red River Expedition of 1870 was a military force of British regulars and Canadian militia led by Colonel Garnet Wolseley to assert Canadian authority at Red River, in present-day Manitoba, after the resistance led by Louis Riel. The troops travelled from Ontario by lake,…

rapperswil.s: Rapperswil is a town on the northern shore of Lake Zürich in the canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland, dominated by its medieval castle.

rudolf-stussi.s: Rudolf Stüssi was burgomaster of Zürich who led the city into alliance with the Habsburgs during the Old Zürich War. He was killed on 22 July 1443 at the Battle of St.

roman-dutch-law.s: Roman-Dutch law is the legal system that developed in the Netherlands in the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries by combining Roman civil law with Dutch custom, and was described by jurists such as Hugo Grotius. Carried to the Cape by the Dutch East India Company, it was kept by…

reginar-iii-count-of-hainaut.s: Reginar III was count of Hainaut in the mid-tenth century, a grandson of Reginar Longneck. His resistance to Otto I's rule in Lotharingia led Archbishop Bruno of Cologne to exile him to Bohemia in 958, where he died, and to divide Hainaut into the counties of Mons and…

reginar-iv-count-of-mons.s: Reginar IV was a son of the exiled Reginar III who fought for decades to recover his family's lands in Hainaut. Helped by his marriage to Hedwig, daughter of the French king Hugh Capet, he regained the county of Mons by the end of the tenth century, restoring the Reginarids,…

robert-i-count-of-flanders.s: Robert the Frisian was count of Flanders from 1071 to 1093. A younger son of Baldwin V, he gained his name by marrying Gertrude of Saxony, widow of the count of Holland, and governing in Frisia.

rhazuns.s: Rhäzüns is a village on the Hinterrhein in the canton of Graubünden, Switzerland. Its castle, one of the oldest in the region, was the centre of a lordship that in 1497 Count Eitel Friedrich II of Zollern exchanged with Maximilian I for the Austrian lordship of Haigerloch.

raymond-iii-pons.s: Raymond III Pons was count of Toulouse from about 924 to about 950. He defeated a Hungarian raid in Languedoc in 924 and is called duke of Aquitaine in some documents, as the house of Toulouse extended its rights in Septimania and Aquitaine.

russo-turkish-war-1735-1739.s: The Russo-Turkish War of 1735–1739 was fought by Russia, joined by Austria from 1737, against the Ottoman Empire and the Crimean Khanate. Russian armies under Münnich invaded Crimea, burning Bakhchysarai, took Azov and Ochakov and won at Stavuchany in 1739, but losses to…

revolt-of-the-comuneros.s: The Revolt of the Comuneros was a rising of Castilian towns in 1520–1521 against the new king Charles I, his Flemish advisers and his tax demands after his election as Holy Roman Emperor. Led by Toledo and a junta of cities, it was crushed at the Battle of Villalar in April 1521.

ramon-bonifaz.s: Ramón Bonifaz was a merchant of Burgos who commanded the fleet of Ferdinand III of Castile at the siege of Seville and is regarded as the first admiral of Castile. In May 1248 his ships broke the pontoon bridge linking Seville to Triana, cutting the city's supply line, and…

rudolf-slansky.s: Rudolf Slánský was General Secretary of the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia from 1945 to 1951 and a leader of the 1948 takeover. Arrested in 1951, he was the chief defendant in a Stalinist show trial in November 1952 with strongly antisemitic overtones, after which he and…

rigsrad.s: The Rigsråd, or Council of the Realm, was the council of the Danish high nobility and, until the Reformation, bishops, which shared power with the king from the later Middle Ages. Each new king signed an accession charter guaranteeing its privileges.

rosenborg-castle.s: Rosenborg Castle is a Renaissance castle in Copenhagen built by Christian IV between 1606 and 1624, first as a summer house in his gardens. It was a favourite residence of the king, who died there in 1648.

reinheitsgebot.s: The Reinheitsgebot ('purity order') is the name given to the Bavarian beer ordinance issued at Ingolstadt on 23 April 1516 by Dukes William IV and Louis X. It allowed only barley, hops and water in beer and also fixed its price.

rennes-cathedral.s: Rennes Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Peter, is the cathedral of Rennes, capital of Brittany. The dukes of Brittany were crowned there in the later Middle Ages, the Dauphin Francis being the last in 1532.

robert-ii-of-france.s: Robert II, called the Pious, was king of France from 996 to 1031, the son of Hugh Capet, with whom he was crowned in 987. He fought for years to win the Duchy of Burgundy after the death of his uncle Henry the Great in 1002, securing it by about 1005.

robert-of-molesme.s: Robert of Molesme was a French monk who founded the abbey of Molesme in 1075 and then, seeking a stricter life, the New Monastery of Cîteaux in 1098. Ordered by the pope to return to Molesme in 1099, he left Cîteaux to Alberic and Stephen Harding, who shaped the Cistercian order.

rudolph-of-france.s: Rudolph was duke of Burgundy from 921 and king of West Francia from 923 until his death in 936, the son of Richard the Justiciar. Elected by the nobles in place of the deposed Charles the Simple, he fought the Vikings and the Magyars and struggled to win recognition in the south.

raoul-duke-of-lorraine.s: Raoul was duke of Lorraine from 1329 to 1346, succeeding his father Frederick IV. A close ally of the French crown, he founded the collegiate church of Saint-Georges in Nancy.

richard-ii-duke-of-normandy.s: Richard II, called the Good, was ruler of Normandy from 996 to 1026, the son of Richard I. He was the first to use the title of duke regularly, put down a peasant revolt early in his reign and promoted monastic reform, bringing William of Volpiano to Fécamp.

robert-curthose.s: Robert Curthose was the eldest son of William the Conqueror and duke of Normandy from 1087. He took part in the First Crusade, pledging Normandy to his brother William Rufus to pay for it.

rollo.s: Rollo was a Viking leader of Scandinavian origin who founded the Norman principality on the lower Seine. After a failed attack on Chartres in 911, King Charles the Simple granted him lands around Rouen, traditionally by the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte, in return for…

ranuccio-i-farnese-duke-of-parma.n: Ranuccio I Farnese, Duke of Parma
ranuccio-i-farnese-duke-of-parma.s: Ranuccio I Farnese was duke of Parma and Piacenza from 1592, the son of Alessandro Farnese. He strengthened ducal power over the nobility, and in 1612 he executed several leading nobles, including Barbara Sanseverino, for an alleged conspiracy and confiscated their estates.

ratibor-i-duke-of-pomerania.s: Ratibor I was a Pomeranian duke of the Griffin dynasty who ruled after the murder of his brother Wartislaw I around 1135 until his death in 1156. He accepted Polish overlordship, raided the Norwegian town of Konghelle in 1135 and supported the Church, founding with his wife…

rega.s: The Rega is a river in Pomerania, north-western Poland, about 170 km long, which flows north into the Baltic Sea near Mrzeżyno. Along its course lie the towns of Łobez, Resko, Płoty and Trzebiatów, where a diet of the Pomeranian estates adopted the Lutheran Reformation in 1534.

royal-netherlands-east-indies-army.s: The Royal Netherlands East Indies Army (KNIL) was the colonial army of the Dutch East Indies, formed in 1830 and separate from the army of the Netherlands. Its soldiers were mainly Javanese, Ambonese and Manadonese under European officers, and it fought the Padri and Aceh wars…

robert-dudley-1st-earl-of-leicester.s: Robert Dudley, 1st Earl of Leicester, was an English courtier and favourite of Elizabeth I. Under the Treaty of Nonsuch she sent him with an English army to aid the Dutch rebels against Spain in 1585, and the States General made him governor-general.

resheph.s: Resheph was a Syrian and Canaanite god of plague, war and the underworld, worshipped from the third millennium BCE, when he appears as Rasap in the archives of Ebla. He was later venerated at Ugarit, in Cyprus and in New Kingdom Egypt, where pharaohs honoured him as a war god,…

revolt-of-the-arrabal.s: The Revolt of the Arrabal was a rising in 818 of the people of the southern suburb (rabad) of Córdoba against the Umayyad emir al-Hakam I, fuelled by taxation and encouraged by Maliki jurists. After it was crushed, the suburb was razed and thousands of its inhabitants were…

rebellion-of-the-alpujarras-1499-1501.s: The first Rebellion of the Alpujarras was a rising of the Muslims of the former Emirate of Granada between 1499 and 1501, provoked by the mass conversions pressed by Cardinal Cisneros in breach of the Treaty of Granada. It began in the Albaicín of Granada and spread to the…

richomer.s: Richomer (died 393) was a Frankish officer who rose to the highest commands of the Roman army. He fought at Adrianople in 378, became commander of the eastern army under Theodosius I and was consul in 384.

reinhard-keiser.s: Reinhard Keiser (1674–1739) was a German composer who worked for most of his career at Hamburg's Oper am Gänsemarkt, which he also directed. He wrote more than sixty operas, among them Croesus and Octavia, and was the leading figure of early German opera.

ritzebuttel.s: Ritzebüttel is a castle and former bailiwick at the mouth of the Elbe, in present-day Cuxhaven. Acquired by Hamburg in 1394, it served for more than five centuries as the city's outpost for protecting shipping and pilotage on the lower Elbe.

rudesheim-am-rhein.s: Rüdesheim am Rhein is a wine town in Hesse, Germany, on the Rhine at the start of the Rhine Gorge, part of the Upper Middle Rhine Valley World Heritage Site. Famous for its Riesling vineyards, it lies below the Niederwald Monument, built in 1877–1883 to commemorate the…

rassemblement-democratique-africain.s: The Rassemblement Démocratique Africain was an inter-territorial political movement founded at a congress in Bamako in October 1946 under Félix Houphouët-Boigny. It had branches in most territories of French West and Equatorial Africa and campaigned for African rights within…

rhine-crisis.s: The Rhine Crisis of 1840 was a diplomatic confrontation in which the French government of Adolphe Thiers, humiliated in the Eastern Question, raised demands for the Rhine as France's eastern frontier. The threat provoked a wave of German national feeling, expressed in…

romila-thapar.s: Romila Thapar is an Indian historian of ancient and early medieval India, long a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi. Her books include studies of Ashoka and the Mauryas, A History of India and Somanatha: The Many Voices of a History, which examines how…

rafael-urdaneta.s: Rafael Urdaneta was a Venezuelan general of the wars of independence and a close ally of Simón Bolívar. He served as minister of war of Gran Colombia and in September 1830 seized power in Bogotá, hoping to recall Bolívar.

reinhard-von-dalwigk.s: Reinhard von Dalwigk was chief minister of the Grand Duchy of Hesse from 1850 to 1871. After the revolution of 1848 he restored conservative government and pursued an anti-Prussian policy, siding with Austria in the war of 1866 and hoping for French support.

russelsheim.s: Rüsselsheim am Main is a town in the German state of Hesse, on the Main west of Frankfurt. In 1862 Adam Opel began making sewing machines there, and the town grew into the home of the Opel car company, whose headquarters and main factory it hosts.

reciprocal-guarantee-of-two-nations.s: The Reciprocal Guarantee of Two Nations was an act adopted by the Great Sejm of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth on 20 October 1791, as an amendment to the Constitution of 3 May. It confirmed the union of Poland and Lithuania as a federation of equal partners and guaranteed…

ruthenian-uniate-church.s: The Ruthenian Uniate Church was formed by the Union of Brest in 1596, when most Orthodox bishops of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth accepted the authority of the pope while keeping the Byzantine rite. It became the church of much of the Ruthenian population of modern…

radio-luxembourg.s: Radio Luxembourg was a commercial radio station broadcasting from the Grand Duchy from 1933, run by the Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Radiodiffusion. Its powerful transmitters reached audiences across Europe, and its English-language service, outside the BBC's monopoly, became…

rtl-group.s: RTL Group is a Luxembourg-based media company and one of Europe's largest broadcasters. It descends from the Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Radiodiffusion, founded in 1931, which ran Radio Luxembourg, and from the 1950s it built television stations under the RTL name in…

rajyapala.s: Rajyapala was a ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty at Kannauj in the early eleventh century, when the empire had shrunk to a small kingdom. When Mahmud of Ghazni marched on Kannauj in December 1018, Rajyapala abandoned the city without a fight, and it was plundered.

ramabhadra.s: Ramabhadra was a Gurjara-Pratihara emperor who reigned briefly in the 830s CE, between his father Nagabhata II and his son Mihira Bhoja. His short reign appears to have been a time of weakness, in which the empire lost ground to its rivals, including the Palas of Bengal,…

rahmanan.s: Rahmanan, "the Merciful", was the name of the single god worshipped by the kings of Himyar after they abandoned the old south Arabian gods around 380 CE. Inscriptions call him Lord of Heaven, or of Heaven and Earth.

ramesseum.s: The Ramesseum is the mortuary temple of the pharaoh Ramesses II on the west bank of the Nile at Thebes, near modern Luxor. Its reliefs depict his campaigns, including the Battle of Kadesh, and it preserves a version of the Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty.

raghavanka.s: Raghavanka was a Kannada poet of the Hoysala period, a nephew and pupil of the poet Harihara. His Harishchandra Kavya, retelling the story of the truthful king Harishchandra, was the first major work in the shatpadi, six-line, metre, which became a standard form of Kannada…

rajaraja-chola-iii.s: Rajaraja Chola III was king of the declining Chola dynasty from 1216 to 1256. Under him the Chola kingdom was overrun by the Pandyas, and around 1231 he was captured by the Kadava chief Kopperunchinga, being freed only through the intervention of the Hoysala king Narasimha II.

ramanatha-hoysala.s: Ramanatha was a Hoysala king who ruled the Tamil territories of the kingdom from Kannanur Kuppam, near Srirangam, after his father Vira Someshvara divided his lands. His rivalry with his half-brother Narasimha III in Karnataka led to war between them.

rudrabhatta.s: Rudrabhatta was a Kannada poet of the Hoysala period, patronised by a minister of the king Veera Ballala II. His Jagannatha Vijaya retells the life of Krishna and is one of the earliest Vaishnava works in Kannada literature.

rabban-sauma.s: Rabban Sauma was a Turkic monk of the Church of the East, born near Khanbaliq (Beijing), who travelled west on pilgrimage and became an envoy of the Ilkhan Arghun. In 1287–1288 he visited Constantinople, Rome, Paris and Gascony, meeting Philip IV of France, Edward I of England…

royal-commentaries-of-the-incas.s: The Comentarios Reales de los Incas is a history of the Inca Empire by Inca Garcilaso de la Vega, the son of a Spanish conquistador and an Inca noblewoman, published in Lisbon in 1609, with a second part on the conquest in 1617. Drawing on his childhood in Cusco and on Spanish…

romance-of-the-western-chamber.s: The Romance of the Western Chamber (Xixiang ji) is a Chinese love story best known through the zaju drama by Wang Shifu of the Yuan dynasty. It tells of the scholar Zhang Sheng and Cui Yingying, who meet in a monastery and, helped by the maid Hongniang, defy her mother.

raja-ali-haji.s: Raja Ali Haji was a Malay scholar, historian and poet of Bugis descent at the court of Riau-Lingga on the island of Penyengat. He completed the Tuhfat al-Nafis, a history of the Malay and Bugis rulers of the region, and wrote the didactic poem Gurindam Dua Belas.

regulations-on-the-siberian-kirgiz.s: The Regulations on the Siberian Kirgiz were a Russian statute of 1822 drafted by Mikhail Speransky as part of his reform of Siberian government; Kirgiz was then the Russian name for the Kazakhs. The statute abolished the office of khan in the Middle Juz and divided its steppe…

radimichians.s: The Radimichians were an East Slavic tribe of the early Middle Ages, living along the Sozh river in what is now eastern Belarus. They paid tribute to the Khazars until Oleg of Kiev brought them under his rule in the 880s, and after a rising they were defeated again by Vladimir…

rudolf-i-of-burgundy.s: Rudolf I, of the Welf family, was the first king of Upper Burgundy. After the fall of the emperor Charles the Fat in 888 he was crowned at the abbey of Saint-Maurice d'Agaune, ruling the lands between the Jura and the Pennine Alps around Lake Geneva.

rupprecht-crown-prince-of-bavaria.s: Rupprecht was the last crown prince of Bavaria, son of Ludwig III. In the First World War he commanded the German 6th Army from 1914 and from 1916 an army group on the Western Front, rising to field marshal.

rudolf-diesel.s: Rudolf Diesel was a German engineer who invented the diesel engine, a compression-ignition engine far more efficient than the steam engines of his day. He patented the design in 1892–1893 and built working engines with the Augsburg engineering works, later part of MAN, between…

rene-magritte.s: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter whose witty images questioned the relation between pictures, words and reality. His works include "The Treachery of Images", with its pipe captioned "This is not a pipe", and "The Son of Man", a man in a bowler hat whose face is…

ravning-bridge.s: The Ravning Bridge was a wooden bridge across the meadows of the Vejle river valley at Ravning Enge in Jutland, Denmark. Tree-ring dating places its construction around 980, under Harald Bluetooth.

ribe.s: Ribe is a town in south-west Jutland, regarded as the oldest town in Denmark. It began as a trading place in the early eighth century, linked to Frisia and the North Sea trade, and Ansgar built one of the first churches in Scandinavia there around 860.

rigsradet.s: The Rigsrådet, or Council of the Realm, was the council of nobles and bishops that shared power with the king in medieval and early modern Denmark. It took shape from the thirteenth century, helped elect kings and imposed coronation charters limiting their power.

roskilde.s: Roskilde is a city on Zealand, Denmark, at the head of the Roskilde Fjord. It was a royal and episcopal centre from the late tenth century, and its cathedral, built from the twelfth century, has been the burial place of Danish monarchs since the fifteenth and is a UNESCO World…

richard-iii-of-england.s: Richard III was king of England from 1483 to 1485, the last king of the House of York. As Duke of Gloucester he took the throne after his nephew Edward V was declared illegitimate, and Edward and his brother, the Princes in the Tower, disappeared.

runnymede.s: Runnymede is a water meadow on the River Thames in Surrey, west of London, between Windsor and Staines. In June 1215 King John met his rebellious barons there and agreed to the charter later called Magna Carta, which bound the king to the law.

rochefort-charente-maritime.s: Rochefort is a town on the Charente river in western France, near the Atlantic coast. richard-arkwright.s: Richard Arkwright was an English inventor and industrialist, often called the father of the factory system. He patented the water frame, a spinning machine driven by water power, in 1769, and from 1771 built a water-powered cotton mill at Cromford in Derbyshire, with housing…

rhodri-molwynog.s: Rhodri Molwynog was a king of Gwynedd in the first half of the eighth century, whose death the Welsh annals record in 754. He belonged to the royal line descended from Cadwallon ap Cadfan.

rhuddlan.s: Rhuddlan is a town in Denbighshire, north-east Wales, at the lowest crossing of the River Clwyd. Long contested between Welsh rulers and the English, it was taken by Owain Gwynedd in 1167, and Edward I built Rhuddlan Castle there from 1277.

royal-hungary.s: Royal Hungary was the part of the medieval Kingdom of Hungary ruled by the Habsburg kings after the Battle of Mohács in 1526, consisting of the northern and western lands. With its capital and coronation city at Pressburg (Bratislava), it formed a frontier against Ottoman…

ruthenians.s: Ruthenians is the historical name for the East Slavic peoples of the former lands of Kievan Rus', used especially for the ancestors of Ukrainians and Rusyns living in the Kingdom of Hungary, Poland-Lithuania and later the Habsburg monarchy. In Hungary they lived mainly in the…

rhadamistus.s: Rhadamistus was an Iberian prince, son of King Pharasmanes I, who seized the kingdom of Armenia in 51 CE after treacherously killing his uncle Mithridates, its Roman-backed king. His rule was challenged by the Parthian candidate Tiridates, and he was driven out within a few…

rufinus-of-aquileia.s: Rufinus of Aquileia was a Latin Christian monk, historian and translator who lived for many years in Egypt and Palestine before returning to Italy. roman-catholic-relief-act-1793.s: The Roman Catholic Relief Act 1793 was a law of the Irish Parliament, passed under pressure from the British government, that gave Catholics the vote in parliamentary elections on the same terms as Protestants and opened most civil and military offices to them. Catholics…

ramoth-gilead.s: Ramoth-gilead was an Iron Age town east of the Jordan in Gilead, often identified with Tell er-Rumeith in northern Jordan. According to the Bible it was a frontier stronghold disputed between Israel and Aram-Damascus in the 9th century BCE.

ramiro-ii-of-aragon.s: Ramiro II, called the Monk, was King of Aragon from 1134 to 1137. A Benedictine monk, he was called from the cloister to succeed his brother Alfonso I the Battler, who had died childless.

repton.s: Repton is a village in south Derbyshire, England, near the River Trent. It was a royal centre of Mercia, with a double monastery whose church crypt became the burial place of kings, among them Æthelbald and Wiglaf.

richard-wellesley-1st-marquess-wellesley.s: Richard Wellesley, 1st Marquess Wellesley (1760–1842), was Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805. royal-palace-of-caserta.s: The Royal Palace of Caserta, north of Naples, was begun in 1752 for Charles of Bourbon to designs by Luigi Vanvitelli. ribera-navarra.s: The Ribera Navarra is the southern lowland region of Navarre along the river Ebro and its tributaries, centred on the city of Tudela. Hot and dry compared with the mountain valleys of the north, it depends on irrigation, much of it inherited from the Muslim period, and is…

ripon.s: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England. A monastery founded there around 660 was given to Wilfrid, who built a stone church whose seventh-century crypt survives beneath the present cathedral.

ruthwell-cross.s: The Ruthwell Cross is an eighth-century Anglo-Saxon stone cross now inside the church of Ruthwell in Dumfriesshire, Scotland. Its carved panels show scenes from the Gospels with Latin inscriptions, and its sides bear runic verses related to the Old English poem The Dream of…

roald-amundsen.s: Roald Amundsen (1872–1928) was a Norwegian polar explorer. He led the first voyage through the Northwest Passage in the Gjøa (1903–1906) and the first expedition to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911, ahead of Robert Falcon Scott.

roros.s: Røros is a mining town in the mountains of central Norway, in Trøndelag. Copper was mined there from 1644 until 1977, making the works one of the main sources of revenue for Denmark-Norway.

rhys-ab-owain.s: Rhys ab Owain was king of Deheubarth in south-west Wales in the 1070s. In 1075 he killed Bleddyn ap Cynfyn, king of Gwynedd and Powys, an act Welsh chroniclers condemned.

rhiwallon-ap-cynfyn.s: Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn was a Welsh king who, with his brother Bleddyn ap Cynfyn, was set up as ruler of Gwynedd and Powys under the overlordship of Edward the Confessor after the death of Gruffudd ap Llywelyn in 1063. The brothers joined English rebels against William the…

robert-of-belleme.s: Robert of Bellême was an Anglo-Norman magnate, son of Roger de Montgomery, with great estates in Normandy and England. He became Earl of Shrewsbury in 1098 and was notorious for his cruelty.

roger-de-montgomery.s: Roger de Montgomery was a Norman noble and close adviser of William the Conqueror. Made Earl of Shrewsbury around 1074, he built castles at Shrewsbury and at Montgomery, which took its name from his Norman home, and led Norman expansion into mid Wales and Powys.

river-vyrnwy.s: The River Vyrnwy (Afon Efyrnwy) is a river of mid Wales that flows east from the Berwyn area through Montgomeryshire to join the Severn near the English border. Its valley was a heartland of medieval Powys, with the mother church at Meifod and the princely court of Mathrafal.

ryangombe.s: Ryangombe is a legendary hero and spirit at the centre of the kubandwa cult of Rwanda and neighbouring lands, known in Burundi as Kiranga. Initiates were possessed by Ryangombe and his companions in rites that offered protection, healing and fertility, and the cult cut across…

roxburgh-castle.s: Roxburgh Castle was a royal castle in the Scottish Borders, on a ridge between the Tweed and the Teviot near Kelso, beside the medieval royal burgh of Roxburgh. It was one of the castles surrendered to England by the Treaty of Falaise in 1174 and was held by the English for…

riksdag-of-vasteras-1527.s: The Riksdag of Västerås of June 1527 was the assembly at which Gustav Vasa, threatening to abdicate, forced the estates to transfer much of the wealth of the church to the crown and to allow the preaching of the Lutheran gospel. Its decisions, set out in the Recess of…

rotterdam.s: Rotterdam is the second-largest city of the Netherlands, on the Nieuwe Maas in the delta of the Rhine and Meuse. It received city rights in 1340 and grew with the Nieuwe Waterweg of 1872 into the largest port in Europe, handling much of the trade of Germany's Rhineland.

ruud-lubbers.s: Ruud Lubbers was a Dutch Christian Democratic politician who served as Prime Minister of the Netherlands from 1982 to 1994. His governments cut public spending and, with the employers and unions, pursued wage moderation under the Wassenaar Agreement, helping the economy to…

river-ness.s: The River Ness is a river in the Scottish Highlands that flows from Loch Ness through Inverness to the Moray Firth. According to Adomnán's Life of Columba, the saint visited the fortress of the Pictish king Bridei son of Maelchon near it in the 560s, and the account of his…

river-avon-hampshire.s: The River Avon is a river in southern England that rises in Wiltshire, flows south through Salisbury and western Hampshire, and reaches the sea at Christchurch Harbour. river-avon-warwickshire.s: The River Avon is a river in the English Midlands that rises in Northamptonshire and flows south-west for about 135 kilometres through Warwickshire, Stratford-upon-Avon and Evesham to join the Severn at Tewkesbury. royal-yugoslav-army.s: The Royal Yugoslav Army was the army of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia, from 1918 to 1945. Built on the Serbian army that had fought in the First World War, it had a mainly Serbian officer corps.

rabatak-inscription.s: The Rabatak inscription is a text in the Bactrian language and Greek script, found in 1993 at Rabatak in Baghlan Province, northern Afghanistan. Issued in the first year of Kanishka's reign, it records the line of Kushan kings from Kujula Kadphises to Kanishka, lists cities…

restored-toungoo-kingdom.s: The Restored Toungoo Kingdom was the Burmese state rebuilt by Nyaungyan Min and his successors after the collapse of the First Toungoo Empire. ranganathaswamy-temple-srirangam.s: The Ranganathaswamy Temple at Srirangam, on an island in the Kaveri River near Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu, is one of the most important shrines of Vishnu and among the largest functioning Hindu temple complexes in the world. royal-malay-regiment.s: The Royal Malay Regiment is the main infantry regiment of the Malaysian Army, founded by the British in 1933 as the Malay Regiment. It fought against the Japanese invasion of 1941–1942, notably at Pasir Panjang in Singapore, and against communist insurgents in the Malayan…

rukun-negara.s: The Rukun Negara ('Principles of the Nation') is Malaysia's national philosophy, proclaimed on 31 August 1970 after the racial riots of 13 May 1969 to foster unity among its peoples. Its five principles are belief in God, loyalty to king and country, the supremacy of the…

renewed-land-ordinance.s: The Renewed Land Ordinance was the constitution imposed by Ferdinand II on Bohemia in 1627 and on Moravia in 1628 after the defeat of the Bohemian Revolt. radama-ii.s: Radama II was king of Madagascar from 1861 to 1863, the son of Ranavalona I. He reversed his mother's policies, freeing Christians, opening the kingdom to foreigners and missionaries and granting vast concessions to Joseph-François Lambert.

ralambo.s: Ralambo was a king of Imerina in the central highlands of Madagascar, traditionally dated to around 1575–1610, the son of Andriamanelo. Royal tradition credits him with giving the kingdom the name Imerina, introducing the royal talismans and the festival of the royal bath, and…

rasoherina.s: Rasoherina was queen of Madagascar from 1863 to 1868, the widow of Radama II, placed on the throne after his murder. Real power passed to the prime minister, first Rainivoninahitriniony and from 1864 Rainilaiarivony, who married her.

reich-security-main-office.s: The Reich Security Main Office (RSHA) was formed in September 1939 by Heinrich Himmler to combine the Security Police, including the Gestapo and the criminal police, with the SS intelligence service, the SD. reichstag-fire-decree.s: The Reichstag Fire Decree was an emergency decree issued by President Paul von Hindenburg on 28 February 1933, the day after the Reichstag building was set on fire. reichswehr.s: The Reichswehr was the armed forces of the Weimar Republic and of Germany's first years under Hitler. The Treaty of Versailles limited it to 100,000 men in the army and 15,000 in the navy, without tanks, heavy artillery or military aircraft.

robert-ley.s: Robert Ley was a Nazi politician who headed the German Labour Front from 1933 to 1945, after the trade unions were dissolved, and was the party's Reich organisation leader. He founded the Strength Through Joy leisure organisation.

richard-white-historian.s: Richard White is an American historian of the American West and of Native American history, long a professor at Stanford University. real-audiencia-of-mexico.s: The Real Audiencia of Mexico was the highest royal court of New Spain, established in 1527. Its first judges, led by Nuño de Guzmán, governed so harshly that the Crown replaced them in 1530 and appointed a viceroy in 1535, who presided over the court.

roman-inquisition.s: The Roman Inquisition was a system of church tribunals founded by Pope Paul III in 1542 and run by a congregation of cardinals in Rome to combat Protestantism and other heresy in Italy. Its best-known case was the trial of Galileo Galilei in 1633.

royal-and-pontifical-university-of-mexic.n: Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico
royal-and-pontifical-university-of-mexic.s: The Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico was founded by a decree of Charles V in 1551 and opened in Mexico City in 1553, one of the first universities in the Americas. robert-muldoon.s: Robert Muldoon was Prime Minister of New Zealand from 1975 to 1984 and also his own finance minister. Leading the National Party, he responded to oil shocks and loss of British markets with heavy state intervention, including the Think Big energy projects and a wage and price…

ruth-richardson.s: Ruth Richardson is a New Zealand politician who was Minister of Finance in Jim Bolger's National government from 1990 to 1993. Her 1991 budget cut welfare benefits, and she pursued tight fiscal policy and labour-market deregulation through the Employment Contracts Act 1991,…

rakvere.s: Rakvere, German Wesenberg, is a town in northern Estonia. Near it on 18 February 1268 the armies of Novgorod and other Russian principalities fought the Livonian Order and the Danish vassals of northern Estonia in the bloody Battle of Wesenberg, which neither side won decisively.

rhescuporis-ii.s: Rhescuporis II was a king of the Sapaean dynasty of Thrace, a brother of Rhoemetalces I. On Rhoemetalces' death around 12 CE Augustus divided the client kingdom between Rhescuporis and his nephew Cotys.

rhoemetalces-i.s: Rhoemetalces I was a Thracian king of the Sapaean dynasty and a Roman client ruler from about 12 BCE. Having sided with Octavian before the Battle of Actium, he was made king of a Thracian kingdom that claimed the Odrysian inheritance, and Roman armies under Lucius Calpurnius…

rajakumar.s: Rajakumar, also known as Yazakumar, was a prince of Pagan and son of King Kyansittha. When his father was dying around 1112 he built a temple in his memory and set up the Myazedi inscription, which records the same text in Pali, Mon, Pyu and Old Burmese.

ramacharita.s: The Ramacharita is a Sanskrit poem written in the twelfth century by Sandhyakara Nandi, in which each verse can be read in two ways: as the story of the god Rama and as the history of the Pala king Ramapala. It is the main source for the revolt of the Kaivartas in northern…

ramavati.s: Ramavati was a capital of the Pala dynasty founded by King Ramapala in Varendra, northern Bengal, after he recovered the region from the Kaivarta rebels in the late eleventh century. It is praised in the Ramacharita and served as the seat of the last Pala kings, but its exact…

roman-campagna.s: The Roman Campagna is the low, undulating plain surrounding Rome in Lazio, Italy. Densely settled in antiquity, it was later given over to great estates and grazing and became malarial and thinly populated, a landscape of ruins painted by artists such as Claude Lorrain and…

richard-nixon.s: Richard Nixon was the 37th president of the United States, from 1969 to 1974. He withdrew American forces from Vietnam, pursued détente with the Soviet Union and, with Henry Kissinger, opened relations with the People's Republic of China, visiting Beijing in February 1972.

red-guards-china.s: The Red Guards were militant student and youth groups mobilised by Mao Zedong at the start of the Cultural Revolution in 1966. They attacked teachers, party officials and 'old' culture, destroying temples, books and artefacts, and soon fought among themselves.

rakow-swietokrzyskie.s: Raków is a village in south-central Poland, founded as a town in 1569. In the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries it was the centre of the Polish Brethren, with an academy and a press that issued the Racovian Catechism in 1605.

renier-de-huy.s: Renier de Huy was a goldsmith and bronze-caster of the Mosan region, active in the early twelfth century. He is credited with the bronze baptismal font now in the church of Saint Bartholomew in Liège, made between about 1107 and 1118, a masterpiece of Romanesque art.

robert-of-thourotte.s: Robert of Thourotte was prince-bishop of Liège from 1240 to 1246, after serving as bishop of Langres. rama-ii.s: Rama II, Phra Phutthaloetla Naphalai, was the second king of the Chakri dynasty of Siam, reigning from 1809 to 1824. A son of Rama I, he presided over a period of peace and revived trade with China, while the court became a centre of the arts.

rama-iii.s: Rama III, Phra Nangklao, was the third king of the Chakri dynasty of Siam, reigning from 1824 to 1851. His reign saw the Burney Treaty with Britain in 1826, the defeat of Anouvong of Vientiane in 1827–1828 and long wars with Vietnam over Cambodia.

ramakien.s: The Ramakien is the Thai national version of the Indian epic Ramayana. Older versions were lost with the fall of Ayutthaya in 1767, and the standard text was composed in 1797 under the direction of King Rama I.

rene-barrientos.s: René Barrientos was a Bolivian air force general who, as vice-president, overthrew President Víctor Paz Estenssoro in November 1964. He ruled Bolivia, as junta leader and then elected president, until his death in a helicopter crash in 1969.

real-audiencia-of-quito.s: The Real Audiencia of Quito was a Spanish colonial court and administrative unit created in 1563, covering most of present-day Ecuador and parts of southern Colombia and northern Peru. It belonged first to the Viceroyalty of Peru and from 1739 to New Granada.

rio-protocol.s: The Rio de Janeiro Protocol was signed on 29 January 1942 by Ecuador and Peru after Peru's victory in the war of 1941, with Argentina, Brazil, Chile and the United States as guarantors. It assigned most of the Amazon territory claimed by Ecuador to Peru.

roque-dalton.s: Roque Dalton was a Salvadoran poet, essayist and revolutionary, regarded as one of the most important Latin American poets of his generation. Imprisoned and exiled for his political activity, he spent years in Mexico, Cuba and Prague, and his works include Poemas clandestinos.

riigikogu.s: The Riigikogu is the single-chamber parliament of Estonia. Created by the constitution of 1920, it held supreme power in the interwar republic, which had no separate presidency.

ruben-blades.s: Rubén Blades is a Panamanian singer, songwriter, actor and politician, one of the leading figures of salsa music. His recordings of the 1970s with Willie Colón, notably the album Siembra of 1978, brought socially conscious lyrics to the genre.
