river-medway.s: The River Medway flows through Kent in south-eastern England to the Thames estuary. In 43 CE the Roman invasion army fought a two-day battle at a crossing of the river, probably near Rochester.

russian-provisional-government.s: The Russian Provisional Government governed Russia from the abdication of Nicholas II in March 1917 until the Bolshevik seizure of power in November 1917. Led first by Prince Georgy Lvov and then by Alexander Kerensky, it granted civil liberties and in September proclaimed…

russo-turkish-wars.s: The Russo-Turkish wars were a series of about a dozen wars between Russia and the Ottoman Empire from the sixteenth century to the First World War. Fought mainly around the Black Sea, in the Balkans and in the Caucasus, they won Russia the northern Black Sea coast, including…

rekidai-hoan.s: The Rekidai Hōan is the collected diplomatic correspondence of the Ryukyu Kingdom, written in classical Chinese and covering the years 1424 to 1867. It contains letters and documents exchanged with China, Korea, Siam, Malacca, Java, Palembang and other states.

rostam.s: Rostam is the greatest hero of Iranian epic, celebrated above all in Ferdowsi's Shahnameh, completed around 1010. Lord of Zabulistan and Sistan and son of Zal, he rides the horse Rakhsh and defends the kings of Iran against their enemies through many generations, and his…

rhenia.s: Rhenia is an uninhabited Greek island in the Cyclades, just west of Delos. Polycrates of Samos captured it in the sixth century BCE and dedicated it to Apollo, binding it to Delos with a chain.

rhoecus.s: Rhoecus was a Greek architect and sculptor of Samos in the sixth century BCE. Herodotus names him as the first architect of the great temple of Hera at the Heraion, one of the first colossal Ionic temples, which he designed with Theodorus.

ribchester.s: Ribchester is a village on the River Ribble in Lancashire, England, on the site of the Roman fort of Bremetennacum. From the later second century it housed a cavalry unit of Sarmatians, descended from the Iazyges sent to Britain by Marcus Aurelius in 175 CE and still recorded…

rila-monastery.s: Rila Monastery is the largest Eastern Orthodox monastery in Bulgaria, in the Rila Mountains south of Sofia, founded in the tenth century by followers of the hermit Saint John of Rila. Its charter from Tsar Ivan Shishman of 1378 survives, and it preserved Bulgarian culture…

renfang.s: The Renfang were a people to the east of the Shang heartland, in the region of present-day Shandong and the Huai River, named in late Shang oracle-bone inscriptions. The last Shang kings, Di Yi and Di Xin, fought long campaigns against them.

ronald-reagan.s: Ronald Reagan was the 40th president of the United States, serving from 1981 to 1989, after careers as a film actor and governor of California. He cut taxes, increased military spending and took a hard line against the Soviet Union, launching the Strategic Defense Initiative,…

russian-revolution.s: The Russian Revolution of 1917 brought down the Russian monarchy and led to the first communist state. The February Revolution in Petrograd forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate and created a Provisional Government, which lost support as Russia stayed in the First World War.

rumi.s: Rumi, Jalal al-Din Muhammad, was a Persian poet, Sufi mystic and scholar born in Balkh in 1207. His family settled in Konya, capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum, in the 1220s, and he taught there until his death in 1273.

rajah-baguinda.s: Rajah Baguinda is a figure of Sulu tradition, a prince said in the Sulu genealogies to have come from Minangkabau in Sumatra around the end of the fourteenth century and to have helped spread Islam in the Sulu archipelago. According to the same tradition, his daughter married…

raga-mulya.s: Raga Mulya, also called Prabu Suryakancana, was by Sundanese tradition the last king of Sunda. He ruled a shrinking inland realm while the sultanates of Banten and Cirebon held the coast, and when Banten's forces took the capital Pakuan Pajajaran in about 1579 the kingdom came…

ronnie-brunswijk.s: Ronnie Brunswijk is a Surinamese Maroon leader and politician, a former soldier and bodyguard of Desi Bouterse who in 1986 founded the Jungle Commando and led it in the interior war against the military regime until 1992. He later founded the General Liberation and Development…

ronald-venetiaan.s: Ronald Venetiaan is a Surinamese mathematician and politician, leader of the National Party of Suriname, who was president of Suriname from 1991 to 1996 and again from 2000 to 2010. His first government, elected after military rule, concluded the 1992 peace accord that ended…

regeneration-switzerland.s: The Regeneration was the period of Swiss history from 1830 to 1848 in which liberal movements, encouraged by the July Revolution in France, won new constitutions in most cantons, introducing popular sovereignty, freedom of the press and equality before the law. Conflict…

royal-marines.s: The Royal Marines are the amphibious infantry of the British Royal Navy, whose origins go back to a regiment raised for sea service in 1664. They have fought in most British wars, from the capture of Gibraltar in 1704 to the Falklands War.

rene-millon.s: René Millon was an American archaeologist who directed the Teotihuacan Mapping Project from 1962, which surveyed the whole ancient city and produced a detailed map of its more than two thousand apartment compounds. His work showed that Teotihuacan was a planned city of perhaps…

ralpachen.s: Ralpachen, also called Tritsuk Detsen, was emperor of Tibet from about 815 to 838. A lavish patron of Buddhism, he promoted the translation of scriptures and the standardisation of terms, and concluded the peace treaty of 821–822 with Tang China, recorded on a bilingual pillar…

red-square.s: Red Square is the main square of Moscow, lying along the eastern wall of the Kremlin between it and the old merchant quarter of Kitay-gorod. Cleared as a market place in the late fifteenth century, it took its name, which in old Russian meant 'beautiful' as well as 'red', in…

richard-chancellor.s: Richard Chancellor was an English navigator who in 1553 sailed with Sir Hugh Willoughby's expedition in search of a north-east passage to China. Separated from the other ships, he reached the White Sea and travelled overland to Moscow, where Ivan IV received him and granted…

raj-singh-i.s: Raj Singh I was Maharana of Mewar from 1652 to 1680. He opposed Aurangzeb's reimposition of the jizya in 1679 and supported the Rathores of Marwar in the Rajput war against the Mughal emperor.

rajsamand-lake.s: Rajsamand Lake is an artificial lake near Kankroli in Rajasthan, created between about 1662 and 1676 by Maharana Raj Singh I of Mewar by damming the Gomati River, partly as famine relief. Its marble embankment, with ornate pavilions and steps, carries the Raj Prashasti, a…

rani-karnavati.s: Rani Karnavati was a queen of Mewar, widow of Rana Sanga and regent for her young son Vikramaditya. When Bahadur Shah of Gujarat besieged Chittor in 1534–1535, she organised its defence and, as the fort fell in March 1535, led the women of Chittor in jauhar.

ratnasimha.s: Ratnasimha was the last ruler of the main Guhila line of Mewar, reigning at Chittor from about 1302. In 1303 the Delhi sultan Alauddin Khalji besieged Chittor for about eight months and took the fort, and Ratnasimha was killed or captured.

rand-revolt.s: The Rand Revolt was an armed uprising of white mineworkers on the Witwatersrand in 1922, sparked by mine owners' plans to cut costs by employing more black workers in semi-skilled jobs. Strikers organised in commandos seized parts of Johannesburg in March, and Jan Smuts's…

reform-act-1832.s: The Reform Act 1832, known as the Great Reform Act, reformed the electoral system of England and Wales. Passed by Earl Grey's Whig government after a political crisis and resistance from the House of Lords, it abolished many rotten and pocket boroughs, gave seats to growing…

royal-and-parliamentary-titles-act-1927.s: The Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act 1927 was an act of the UK Parliament that changed the formal name of the state to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, recognising the separation of the Irish Free State in 1922. It also allowed the royal style and…

representation-of-the-people-act-1918.s: The Representation of the People Act 1918 extended the vote to almost all men over 21 and, for the first time, to most women over 30 in the United Kingdom. Passed at the end of the First World War, it nearly tripled the electorate, and at the first election held under it, in…

roman-catholic-relief-act-1829.s: The Roman Catholic Relief Act 1829 granted Catholic emancipation in the United Kingdom, allowing Catholics to sit in Parliament and hold most public offices. It was passed by Wellington's government after Daniel O'Connell's election for County Clare in 1828 raised fears of…

representation-of-the-people-act-1884.s: The Representation of the People Act 1884, known as the Third Reform Act, extended to the counties the household franchise that the Act of 1867 had given the boroughs. Passed by Gladstone's second government, it roughly doubled the electorate to about five million men, and was…

rambagh-palace.s: The Rambagh Palace is a former royal residence in Jaipur, Rajasthan. Built in 1835 as a garden house and later enlarged into a palace, it became the main residence of Maharaja Man Singh II in 1925, and in 1957 it was converted into a luxury hotel, one of the first palace…

rajasthan-day.s: Rajasthan Day is a public holiday in the Indian state of Rajasthan, celebrated on 30 March. It commemorates the inauguration in 1949 of the United State of Greater Rajasthan, when the major princely states of Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaisalmer joined the union, the…

rajasthan-high-court.s: The Rajasthan High Court is the high court of the Indian state of Rajasthan, inaugurated in August 1949 with its principal seat at Jodhpur, a location chosen to balance Jodhpur against the state capital at Jaipur. It replaced the separate high courts of the former princely…

rajputana.s: Rajputana was the historical name of the region of north-western India roughly corresponding to present-day Rajasthan, so called by the British after its Rajput ruling dynasties. Under British rule it consisted of some two dozen princely states, including Mewar, Marwar, Jaipur…

republican-party-united-states.s: The Republican Party is one of the two major political parties of the United States, founded in 1854 by opponents of the expansion of slavery into the western territories. Its first successful presidential candidate, Abraham Lincoln, was elected in 1860, and it dominated…

romulo-betancourt.s: Rómulo Betancourt was a Venezuelan politician, founder of the social-democratic party Democratic Action, often called the father of Venezuelan democracy. He headed a revolutionary junta from 1945 to 1948 and, after the fall of Marcos Pérez Jiménez, was elected president for…

revolution-of-the-reforms.s: The Revolution of the Reforms was a military uprising in Venezuela in 1835–1836 against the civilian president José María Vargas. Led by officers of the independence wars, among them Santiago Mariño, it demanded constitutional reforms, a federal system and privileges for the…

romulo-gallegos.s: Rómulo Gallegos was a Venezuelan novelist and politician, author of Doña Bárbara (1929), a classic of Latin American literature about the struggle between civilisation and barbarism on the llanos. Elected president in December 1947 as the Democratic Action candidate in the…

real-audiencia-of-lima.s: The Real Audiencia of Lima was the highest royal court of the Viceroyalty of Peru, created in 1542 under the New Laws and installed in Lima in 1544. Presided over by the viceroy, it heard appeals, advised on government and ruled the viceroyalty when the office of viceroy was…

real-felipe-fortress.s: The Real Felipe Fortress is a large pentagonal fortress at Callao, the port of Lima, built by the Spanish between 1747 and 1774 after the earthquake and tsunami of 1746 destroyed the town. Named after Philip V, it was the main defence of the coast of the Viceroyalty of Peru.

rose-of-lima.s: Rose of Lima was a Peruvian lay member of the Dominican order known for her severe asceticism, prayer and care for the poor and sick of Lima. Canonised by Pope Clement X in 1671, she was the first person born in the Americas to be declared a saint.

rajadhiraja-chola.s: Rajadhiraja Chola was a Chola king, the eldest son of Rajendra I, who was co-ruler from 1018 and sole ruler from 1044 to 1054. A warlike king, he campaigned in Sri Lanka and repeatedly against the Western Chalukyas, and claimed to have sacked their capital Kalyani.

rajendra-chola-ii.s: Rajendra Chola II was a Chola king who reigned from about 1052 to 1064, the younger brother of Rajadhiraja I. When Rajadhiraja was killed at the Battle of Koppam in 1054, he took command, rallied the army and was crowned on the battlefield.

ranna.s: Ranna was a Kannada poet of the late tenth century, one of the 'three gems' of early Kannada literature with Pampa and Ponna. Born into a family of bangle-sellers, he became court poet of the Western Chalukya kings Tailapa II and Satyashraya with the title Kavichakravarti.

records-of-the-three-kingdoms.s: The Records of the Three Kingdoms (Sanguo zhi) is the official history of the Three Kingdoms period of China (220–280 CE), written by Chen Shou in the late third century. Its accounts of the states of Wei, Shu and Wu, expanded by Pei Songzhi's fifth-century commentary, are the…

ruyan.s: Ruyan was a mountainous region of western Tabaristan, on the northern slopes of the Alborz in what is now Mazandaran, Iran, later known as Rustamdar. Its local princes, above all the Paduspanids, kept power there for centuries under successive overlords, and in 864 its people…

ramapala.s: Ramapala was king of the Pala dynasty of eastern India from about 1077 to 1130. He recovered northern Bengal (Varendra) from the Kaivarta rebels with the help of a coalition of feudatory chiefs, founded a new capital at Ramavati, and briefly restored Pala power.

romagna.s: Romagna is a historical region of northern Italy between the Apennines, the Adriatic and the lower Po, now the eastern part of Emilia-Romagna. Its towns, among them Ravenna, Rimini, Forlì, Faenza and Cesena, were held by local lords under papal overlordship until Cesare Borgia…

rozafa-castle.s: Rozafa Castle is a fortress on a rocky hill above Shkodër in northern Albania, near the meeting of the Buna and Drin rivers and Lake Shkodër. Originally an Illyrian stronghold, it was rebuilt by Venice and taken by the Ottomans after the siege of 1478–79.

raja-biru.s: Raja Biru, 'the Blue Queen', ruled the Malay sultanate of Pattani from 1616 to 1624, succeeding her sister Raja Hijau. She was the second of four queens who governed Pattani in succession from 1584, a period when it was a prosperous port trading with Chinese, Japanese and…

raja-ungu.s: Raja Ungu, 'the Purple Queen', ruled the Malay sultanate of Pattani from 1624 to 1635, the third of four queens who governed it in succession. Unlike her sisters, she took a defiant stance towards Siam, abandoning Siamese titles and tribute, which brought Siamese attacks on…

raja-kuning.s: Raja Kuning, 'the Yellow Queen', was the last of the four queens who ruled the Malay sultanate of Pattani in succession, reigning from 1635. A daughter of Raja Ungu, she made peace with Siam, which had attacked Pattani under her mother, and kept up its trade.

russo-persian-treaty-of-friendship-1921.s: The Russo-Persian Treaty of Friendship was signed in Moscow on 26 February 1921 between Soviet Russia and Persia. Russia renounced tsarist concessions, debts and privileges and agreed to withdraw its forces from northern Iran, ending its support for the Soviet republic in Gilan.

ruvo-di-puglia.s: Ruvo di Puglia is a town in the Metropolitan City of Bari in Apulia, southern Italy, on the site of ancient Rubi, a Peucetian centre. Its tombs have yielded large numbers of painted Greek and Apulian vases of the 5th and 4th centuries BCE, many preserved in the town's Jatta…

ramon-magsaysay.s: Ramon Magsaysay was a Filipino statesman, president of the Philippines from 1953 until his death in an air crash in 1957. As secretary of national defence from 1950 he reformed the army and combined military pressure with offers of land and amnesty to defeat the Hukbalahap…

reamker.s: The Reamker is the Cambodian version of the Indian epic Ramayana, telling the story of Preah Ream (Rama) and his rescue of his wife Sita from the demon king Krong Reap. Known in written form from the 16th and 17th centuries, it was adapted to Theravada Buddhist values and is…

rhon.s: The Rhön is a range of low volcanic mountains in central Germany, where Hesse, Bavaria and Thuringia meet. Its highest peak is the Wasserkuppe, at 950 metres, known as the birthplace of gliding.

romansh.s: Romansh is a Romance language spoken in the canton of Graubünden in eastern Switzerland, descended from the Latin of the Roman province of Raetia. It has several regional varieties and a common written standard, Rumantsch Grischun, created in 1982.

ratzeburg.s: Ratzeburg is a town on an island in the Ratzeburg Lake in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. Henry the Lion founded a bishopric there in 1154, and its Romanesque brick cathedral survives.

rotenburg-an-der-wumme.s: Rotenburg an der Wümme is a town in Lower Saxony, Germany, between Bremen and Hamburg. The prince-bishops of Verden built a castle there in the late 12th century to guard the crossing of the Wümme, and it served as their main residence for most of the later Middle Ages and…

rethel.s: Rethel is a small town on the Aisne in the Ardennes department of north-eastern France. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of the counts of Rethel, and the county later passed to the dukes of Nevers and in the 16th century to the Gonzaga-Nevers family, who held it as a duchy.

roman-mikhailovich-of-bryansk.s: Roman Mikhailovich, called the Old, was a son of Prince Mikhail of Chernigov, killed by the Mongols in 1246. He made Bryansk the seat of the leading principality of the Chernigov lands and ruled it into the 1280s.

robert-ii-of-capua.s: Robert II was the last independent Norman Prince of Capua, of the Drengot family, ruling from 1127. He joined the baronial and papal opposition to Roger II of Sicily, who drove him out in 1135 and gave Capua to his own son.

reapers-war.s: The Reapers' War was a revolt of Catalonia against the government of Philip IV of Spain. Provoked by the billeting of royal troops and the policies of the Count-Duke of Olivares, it began with the killing of the viceroy by reapers in Barcelona in June 1640.

rurik-rostislavich.s: Rurik Rostislavich was a prince of the Smolensk branch of the Rurikids who held the throne of Kiev several times between 1173 and 1210. In 1203, allied with the Olgovichi and the Cumans, he sacked Kiev during his feud with Roman the Great, who later forced him to become a monk.

rainier-iii-prince-of-monaco.s: Rainier III was Prince of Monaco from 1949 to 2005, the longest reign in its history. He enlarged the principality through land reclamation, developed it as a banking and tourism centre and granted the constitution of 1962.

raimbaut-d-orange.s: Raimbaut d'Orange was a Provençal troubadour and lord of part of the county of Orange. About forty of his poems survive, many in the difficult trobar clus style, and he exchanged songs with other troubadours such as Giraut de Bornelh.

rogneda-of-polotsk.s: Rogneda of Polotsk was the daughter of Rogvolod, ruler of Polotsk. According to the Primary Chronicle, Vladimir of Novgorod, later Vladimir the Great, took Polotsk around 978, killed her father and brothers and forced her to marry him.

rogvolod.s: Rogvolod was a 10th-century ruler of Polotsk and the first prince of the town named in the Rus' chronicles, which say he had come 'from overseas', probably from Scandinavia. When he refused the suit of Vladimir of Novgorod for his daughter Rogneda, Vladimir captured Polotsk…

rostov.s: Rostov, also called Rostov Veliky, is a town on Lake Nero in Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia, and one of the oldest towns of north-eastern Rus', first recorded in 862. It was the early centre of the Rostov-Suzdal land, the seat of a bishop and later of a separate principality, which…

radelchis-i-of-benevento.s: Radelchis I was Lombard Prince of Benevento from 839 to 851. A former treasurer, he seized power after the murder of Prince Sicard, provoking a long civil war with Sicard's brother Siconulf, in which both sides hired Muslim mercenaries.

remaclus.s: Remaclus was a 7th-century monk and missionary from Aquitaine, first abbot of Solignac and later active as a bishop in the Meuse region. With land granted by King Sigebert III of Austrasia he founded the twin abbeys of Stavelot and Malmedy in the Ardennes around 650, which…

rededya.s: Rededya was a prince of the Kasogs, the Circassians of the north-western Caucasus. According to the Primary Chronicle, in 1022 he met Mstislav of Tmutarakan in single combat to decide a war, and Mstislav won and killed him, taking his family and lands.

reginald-grey-3rd-baron-grey-de-ruthyn.n: Reginald Grey, 3rd Baron Grey de Ruthyn
reginald-grey-3rd-baron-grey-de-ruthyn.s: Reginald Grey, 3rd Baron Grey de Ruthyn, was an English marcher lord holding Ruthin in north-east Wales. His land dispute with his neighbour Owain Glyndŵr, and Glyndŵr's failure to obtain justice, helped spark the Welsh revolt of 1400.

reich-protector.s: Reich Protector, in German Reichsprotektor, was the title of the highest German official in the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia from 1939 to 1945, who held real power over the nominal Czech government. The post was held by Konstantin von Neurath, with Reinhard Heydrich…

rebellion-losses-bill.s: The Rebellion Losses Bill was a law passed by the Province of Canada in 1849 to compensate residents of Canada East whose property had been damaged during the rebellions of 1837–1838. Tory opponents claimed it rewarded rebels, and when Governor General Lord Elgin signed it, a…

robert-baldwin.s: Robert Baldwin was a lawyer and Reform politician of Upper Canada and Canada West, the leading advocate of responsible government. With Louis-Hippolyte LaFontaine he led the ministry of 1848 to 1851, which established that the cabinet must keep the confidence of the elected…

robert-eden-governor-of-maryland.n: Sir Robert Eden, 1st Baronet, of Maryland
robert-eden-governor-of-maryland.s: Sir Robert Eden was the last colonial governor of Maryland, serving from 1769 to 1776. Married to a sister of the last Lord Baltimore, he tried to keep the peace as revolutionary committees took power, and he left the province peacefully in June 1776.

rutgers-university.s: Rutgers University is the state university of New Jersey, founded in 1766 as Queen's College by ministers of the Dutch Reformed Church. Based in New Brunswick, it was renamed in 1825 after the benefactor Henry Rutgers and became the state university in 1945.

regulator-movement.s: The Regulator Movement was an uprising of backcountry farmers in North Carolina, with a parallel movement in South Carolina, in the late 1760s and early 1770s. In North Carolina the Regulators protested against corrupt officials, excessive fees and unequal taxes, and turned to…

red-river-colony.s: The Red River Colony was a settlement on the Red and Assiniboine rivers in present-day Manitoba, founded by Lord Selkirk in 1812 on land granted by the Hudson's Bay Company. It grew into a community of Métis, Scottish settlers and fur traders centred on Upper Fort Garry.

renault.s: Renault is a French car maker founded in 1899 by Louis Renault and his brothers at Boulogne-Billancourt near Paris. It built taxis, lorries and tanks in the First World War.

relacion-de-michoacan.s: The Relación de Michoacán is a manuscript of about 1540, compiled by the Franciscan friar Jerónimo de Alcalá from the accounts of Purépecha nobles and priests for Viceroy Antonio de Mendoza. Illustrated by native painters, it records the history, religion and government of the…

riobamba.s: Riobamba is a city in the central highlands of Ecuador, capital of Chimborazo Province. Founded by the Spanish in 1534 in the land of the Puruhá, it was the first Spanish city in what is now Ecuador.

rajyavardhana.s: Rajyavardhana was a king of the Pushyabhuti dynasty of Thanesar and the elder brother of Harsha. On the death of his father Prabhakaravardhana around 605 he marched against the king of Malwa, who had killed his brother-in-law, the Maukhari ruler of Kannauj, and defeated him,…

rajah-humabon.s: Rajah Humabon was the ruler of Cebu, then known as Sugbu, in the central Philippines when Ferdinand Magellan's expedition arrived in April 1521. He made a blood compact with Magellan and was baptised with his wife and hundreds of followers, taking the name Carlos, and his wife…

rajkumar-college-rajkot.s: Rajkumar College is a school in Rajkot, Gujarat, India, founded in 1868 under British auspices to educate the sons of the princely rulers and chiefs of Kathiawar. Modelled on English public schools, it trained generations of princes, among them the cricketer Ranjitsinhji, and…

robert-greville-2nd-baron-brooke.s: Robert Greville, 2nd Baron Brooke, was an English Puritan nobleman and Parliamentarian. With Viscount Saye and Sele and others he obtained the Warwick Patent in 1632 for land on the Connecticut River, where the Saybrook Colony, named after the two lords, was founded in 1635.

ramanathaswamy-temple.s: The Ramanathaswamy Temple is a Hindu temple to Shiva on Rameswaram island in Tamil Nadu, India, one of the twelve jyotirlingas and a major pilgrimage site linked with Rama's return from Lanka. Its present structure was largely built from the 12th century onward, and the…

raza-library.s: The Raza Library in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, India, is a library of Indo-Islamic manuscripts and art that grew from the collection of Nawab Faizullah Khan, ruler of Rampur from 1774 to 1794, and was enlarged by later nawabs. It holds thousands of Arabic, Persian and Urdu…

rano-raraku.s: Rano Raraku is a volcanic crater on Rapa Nui (Easter Island) whose compressed volcanic ash was the quarry for nearly all of the island's moai statues. Hundreds of moai remain on its slopes, some standing buried to their shoulders and others unfinished in the rock, showing…

rachakonda.s: Rachakonda is a hill fort in Telangana, India, south-east of Hyderabad. From the late 14th century it was the capital of the Recherla Nayakas, Velama rulers of Telangana, whose kings such as Sarvajna Singabhupala patronised Sanskrit and Telugu learning there.

rasarnava-sudhakara.s: The Rasarnava Sudhakara is a Sanskrit treatise on dramaturgy and poetics attributed to Sarvajna Singabhupala, a Recherla Nayaka king of Rachakonda in the 14th century. It analyses rasa, the aesthetic emotion evoked by drama, together with characters, plot construction and the…

rajahmundry.s: Rajahmundry, officially Rajamahendravaram, is a city on the Godavari River in Andhra Pradesh, India. It was a centre of the Eastern Chalukyas, the seat of a branch of the Reddi kings in the 14th and 15th centuries, and later passed to the Gajapatis, the Qutb Shahis and the…

rennes.s: Rennes is the capital of Brittany in north-western France, at the confluence of the Ille and the Vilaine. It began as Condate, chief town of the Gaulish Redones, and became a Roman civitas capital.

robert-semple.s: Robert Semple was an American-born merchant and travel writer who became governor-in-chief of the Hudson's Bay Company's territories in 1815. Sent to the Red River Colony amid its conflict with the North West Company and the Métis, he was killed together with about twenty of…

rehoboth-namibia.s: Rehoboth is a town in the Hardap Region of central Namibia, south of Windhoek. The Basters, a community of mixed Cape Dutch and Khoekhoe descent, settled there in 1870 and governed it under their own kaptein, council and laws.

reichskommissar.s: A Reichskommissar, or Reich Commissioner, was in Nazi Germany an official appointed to govern an occupied territory as a civil administrator answerable directly to Hitler. During the Second World War Reichskommissariats were set up in Norway, the Netherlands, Ostland and…

reich-ministry-for-the-occupied-eastern-.n: Reich Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories
reich-ministry-for-the-occupied-eastern-.s: The Reich Ministry for the Occupied Eastern Territories was the Nazi German ministry created in July 1941 under Alfred Rosenberg to govern Soviet lands placed under civil administration. It oversaw the Reichskommissariats of Ostland and Ukraine, though the SS, the army and the…

rumbula-massacre.s: The Rumbula massacre was the killing of about 25,000 Jews in Rumbula forest near Riga on 30 November and 8 December 1941. Most victims came from the Riga ghetto, together with about a thousand Jews deported from Germany, and were shot by Einsatzgruppe A under Friedrich Jeckeln…

revolutionary-armed-forces-of-colombia.s: The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) was a Marxist guerrilla group founded in 1964 by Manuel Marulanda and others from peasant self-defence groups. Increasingly financed by kidnapping and the drug trade, it fought the Colombian state for more than five decades.

ramon-grau-san-martin.s: Ramón Grau San Martín was a Cuban physician and politician who headed the revolutionary 'Hundred Days' government of 1933–1934, which decreed labour and social reforms before Fulgencio Batista forced him out. He founded the Auténtico Party and was elected president in 1944,…

robert-william-wilcox.s: Robert William Wilcox was a Native Hawaiian soldier and politician who led armed risings in 1889 against the Bayonet Constitution and in January 1895 against the Republic of Hawaii, aiming to restore Queen Liliʻuokalani. Trained at a military academy in Italy, he was sentenced…

rajendra-prasad.s: Rajendra Prasad was an Indian independence leader and lawyer from Bihar who became the first President of India, serving from 1950 to 1962. A close associate of Mahatma Gandhi from the Champaran campaign of 1917 and a leader of the Indian National Congress, he presided over…

rizal-province.s: Rizal is a province of the Philippines on Luzon, immediately east of Manila, named after the national hero José Rizal. It was created by the American colonial government in 1901 from parts of the former provinces of Manila and Morong.

rhenish-german-national-convention.s: The Rhenish-German National Convention was an assembly elected under French supervision in the territories on the left bank of the Rhine occupied by French revolutionary armies. Meeting in Mainz from 17 March 1793, it proclaimed a free state from Landau to Bingen, known as the…

rio-grande-do-norte.s: Rio Grande do Norte is a state in north-eastern Brazil on the Atlantic coast, at the north-eastern corner of South America, with its capital at Natal. Colonised by the Portuguese from 1598, when the Fort of the Three Kings was built at Natal, it was held by the Dutch from 1633…

rab.s: Rab is an island of Croatia in the Kvarner Gulf of the northern Adriatic, with a medieval town of the same name known for its four bell towers. In Roman times it was a municipium called Arba, and it later belonged in turn to Byzantium, the Croatian-Hungarian kingdom and, from…

rivonia-trial.s: The Rivonia Trial was held in Pretoria in 1963–1964 against leaders of the African National Congress and its armed wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe, after a police raid on their hideout at Liliesleaf Farm in Rivonia, near Johannesburg. Nelson Mandela used his statement from the dock to…

recep-tayyip-erdogan.s: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is a Turkish politician who co-founded the Justice and Development Party (AKP) and has led Turkey since 2003, as prime minister until 2014 and then as president. A former mayor of Istanbul, he oversaw rapid economic growth in his first decade and opened…

rialto.s: The Rialto is the central island group and district of Venice on the Grand Canal, where the seat of government moved in the early 9th century after Pepin of Italy's attack in 810. It became Venice's commercial heart, with its market, banks and merchants' meeting places.

ramchandra-singh-of-rewa.s: Ramchandra Singh was a Baghel raja of Bandhavgarh in the 16th century, ruling the region that became the state of Rewa. He was a celebrated patron of music, and the singer Tansen served at his court until the Mughal emperor Akbar summoned him to Agra in the 1560s.

reggio-calabria.s: Reggio Calabria is the largest city of Calabria in southern Italy, on the Strait of Messina facing Sicily. It was founded as the Greek colony of Rhegion in the 8th century BCE and later became the Roman Rhegium.

riau-malay.s: Riau Malay is the variety of Malay spoken in the Riau archipelago and the old Johor-Riau sultanate. Cultivated as a literary language at the Riau-Lingga court in the 19th century, it was taken by Dutch colonial scholars as the standard form of Malay, and it later became the…

rohilkhand.s: Rohilkhand is a region of western Uttar Pradesh, India, east of the Ganges, centred on Bareilly, Moradabad and Rampur. It is named after the Rohilla Afghans who settled and ruled it in the 18th century.

rohillas.s: The Rohillas were Pashtun (Afghan) soldiers and settlers who came to northern India from the late 17th century and settled in the Katehr region, which became known as Rohilkhand. Under Ali Mohammed Khan and Hafiz Rahmat Khan they built a state in the decline of the Mughal Empire.

rohilla-war.s: The Rohilla War of 1773–1774 was a campaign in which Shuja-ud-Daula, Nawab of Awadh, aided by East India Company troops lent by Warren Hastings, invaded Rohilkhand. The Rohilla leader Hafiz Rahmat Khan was defeated and killed at Miranpur Katra in April 1774, and most of…

roman-forum.s: The Roman Forum was the central public square of ancient Rome, in the valley between the Palatine and Capitoline hills. Drained and paved from the 7th century BCE, it became the centre of the city's political, religious and commercial life, surrounded by temples, basilicas,…

rebellion-of-the-barrios.s: The Rebellion of the Barrios was an uprising of the neighbourhoods of Quito in 1765 against new Bourbon taxes, especially a royal monopoly on cane liquor and stricter collection of the sales tax. Crowds drove out the authorities and the city governed itself for months before…

rueda-de-jalon.s: Rueda de Jalón is a village on the Jalón River west of Zaragoza in Aragon, Spain, below a ruined Islamic castle. After the Almoravids took Zaragoza in 1110 the exiled Hudid dynasty held out there, until Ahmad Sayf al-Dawla (Zafadola) handed it to Alfonso VII of Castile in the…

red-river-resistance.s: The Red River Resistance was the rising of the Métis of the Red River Settlement in 1869–1870 against the transfer of Rupert's Land to Canada without their consent. Led by Louis Riel, they set up a provisional government and negotiated the Manitoba Act of 1870, which created…

russian-american-company.s: The Russian-American Company was a state-chartered trading company that held a monopoly over the fur trade and governed Russian America from 1799 until 1867. Under managers such as Alexander Baranov it ruled from Kodiak and Sitka, extended its posts to California at Fort Ross,…

rodez.s: Rodez is a town in southern France, the capital of the Aveyron department, on a hill above the Aveyron River. As Segodunum it was the chief town of the Gallic Ruteni, and in the Middle Ages it was the seat of a bishop and of the counts of Rodez.

rwandan-patriotic-front.s: The Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF) is a political party and former rebel movement founded in Uganda in 1987 by Rwandan Tutsi exiles. Under Fred Rwigyema and then Paul Kagame it invaded Rwanda in 1990, and in July 1994 it defeated the government forces and ended the genocide…

rwandan-revolution.s: The Rwandan Revolution, or Hutu Revolution, was a period of violence and political change in Rwanda from 1959 to 1961 that ended the Tutsi-led monarchy. Beginning with attacks on Tutsi in November 1959, it brought the Hutu party Parmehutu to power with Belgian support,…

ryukyuans.s: The Ryukyuans are the Indigenous people of the Ryukyu Islands between Kyushu and Taiwan, today mostly part of Okinawa Prefecture in Japan. They formed the Ryukyu Kingdom, which traded widely with China, Japan and South-East Asia, and they speak Ryukyuan languages related to…

ryuzoji-clan.s: The Ryūzōji were a samurai family of Hizen province in Kyushu, originally vassals of the Shōni. Under Ryūzōji Takanobu they overthrew the Shōni and in the 1570s and early 1580s became one of the three great powers of Kyushu beside the Ōtomo and Shimazu.

rieti.s: Rieti, ancient Reate, is a city in Lazio in central Italy, in a fertile basin of the Velino river. It was a chief town of the Sabines and passed under Roman rule in 290 BCE; Manius Curius Dentatus later drained part of the nearby marshes by cutting a channel that created the…

romulus.s: Romulus is the legendary founder and first king of Rome, said to have been suckled with his twin brother Remus by a she-wolf. Roman tradition dated the founding of the city to 753 BCE, told how Romulus killed Remus, and credited him with the abduction of the Sabine women and a…

ranquel.s: The Ranquel, or Rankülche, are an indigenous people of the central Argentine pampas, formed in the 18th century from Mapuche-speaking and other groups. Living by horse herding and raiding, they were allies and rivals of Juan Calfucurá's Salinas Grandes confederation and are…

rudaki.s: Rudaki was a Persian poet at the Samanid court of Bukhara, often called the father of Persian poetry. Born near Panjakent in modern Tajikistan, he enjoyed the patronage of the emir Nasr II and is said to have composed a vast body of verse, though only a small part survives.

ragnit.s: Ragnit, now the town of Neman in the Kaliningrad region of Russia, lies on the south bank of the Neman river. The Teutonic Order built a castle there in 1289 on the site of a Scalovian stronghold, and it became a base for campaigns against Lithuania.

ramon-caceres.s: Ramón Cáceres was a Dominican politician who was president of the Dominican Republic from the end of 1905 until 1911. As a young man he took part in the assassination of the dictator Ulises Heureaux in 1899.

revolution-of-ayutla.s: The Revolution of Ayutla was a liberal uprising in Mexico against the dictatorship of Antonio López de Santa Anna, launched in March 1854 under the Plan of Ayutla, proclaimed in Guerrero with the backing of Juan Álvarez and Ignacio Comonfort. The revolt spread across the…

river-tweed.s: The River Tweed flows about 156 km from the Southern Uplands of Scotland to the North Sea at Berwick-upon-Tweed. For part of its lower course it marks the border between Scotland and England.

resava-school.s: The Resava school was a Serbian literary and scribal school of the early 15th century, centred on the Manasija monastery in the Resava valley founded by the despot Stefan Lazarević. Its scholars, among them Constantine of Kostenets, reformed the spelling of Serbian Church…

ramachandra-of-devagiri.s: Ramachandra was the last major king of the Seuna Yadava dynasty, ruling from Devagiri from 1271. In 1296 Alauddin Khalji raided Devagiri and forced him to pay a huge tribute.

romny-culture.s: The Romny culture was an archaeological culture of the 8th to 10th centuries on the left bank of the Dnieper in present-day Ukraine and Russia. Named after finds at Romny on the Sula, it is known for fortified hilltop settlements, half-sunken houses and moulded pottery.

rashid-bin-humaid-al-nuaimi-i.n: Rashid bin Humaid Al Nuaimi I
rashid-bin-humaid-al-nuaimi-i.s: Rashid bin Humaid Al Nuaimi I was the founder of the Sheikhdom of Ajman on the Trucial Coast. A leader of the Na'im tribe, he took the coastal fort of Ajman in 1816 with the support of the Qawasim of Sharjah and established the dynasty that still rules the emirate.

ras-al-khaimah.s: Ras al-Khaimah is a port city on the northern coast of the United Arab Emirates and capital of the emirate of the same name. It became the main base of the Al Qasimi in the 18th century and was attacked by British expeditions in 1809 and 1819.

royal-air-force.s: The Royal Air Force is the air force of the United Kingdom, founded on 1 April 1918 as the world's first independent air service. Between the wars it policed parts of the Middle East from airfields across Iraq and the Gulf, including Sharjah, on the air route to India.

romance-of-the-three-kingdoms.s: Romance of the Three Kingdoms is a Chinese historical novel attributed to Luo Guanzhong in the 14th century, one of the four classic novels of Chinese literature. It dramatises the fall of the Han dynasty and the wars of Wei, Shu and Wu, mixing history with legend.

ramgarhia-misl.s: The Ramgarhia misl was one of the Sikh confederacies of 18th-century Punjab, named after the fort of Ramgarh at Amritsar and led by Jassa Singh Ramgarhia. It held territory around Batala and in the Jalandhar Doab and was a rival of the Ahluwalia and Kanhaiya misls.

raghubir-sinh.s: Raghubir Sinh (1908–1991) was an Indian historian and heir apparent (Maharaj Kumar) of the princely state of Sitamau in Malwa. He wrote on the history of Malwa and the Rajputs and edited Persian and Rajasthani sources for the Mughal and Maratha periods.

rawanduz.s: Rawanduz is a town in Erbil Governorate in Iraqi Kurdistan, set on a rock above the deep gorge of the Rawanduz river near the Gali Ali Beg canyon. It was the capital of the Kurdish Soran emirate, which under Mir Muhammad Kor in the early 19th century made it a centre of arms…

ruscino.s: Ruscino was an ancient settlement at Château-Roussillon, just east of Perpignan in southern France, and the chief town of the Sordones. An oppidum from the 6th century BCE, it was where Gallic chiefs met Hannibal in 218 BCE, according to Livy, and later became a Roman town…

roussillon.s: Roussillon is a historical region of southern France on the Mediterranean, at the eastern end of the Pyrenees, corresponding mainly to the department of Pyrénées-Orientales, with its capital at Perpignan. A Carolingian county and later part of the Crown of Aragon and the…

rhodesian-front.s: The Rhodesian Front was a white conservative party in Southern Rhodesia, founded in 1962, which won that year's election on a platform of opposing majority rule. Under Ian Smith it made the Unilateral Declaration of Independence in 1965 and governed Rhodesia through the long…

river-oykel.s: The River Oykel is a river of the northern Scottish Highlands, rising near Ben More Assynt and flowing east to the Kyle of Sutherland and the Dornoch Firth. For much of its course it forms the boundary between the historic counties of Sutherland and Ross-shire, and it is noted…

rastatt.s: Rastatt is a town in Baden-Württemberg, south-western Germany, on the Murg near the Rhine. From 1700 Margrave Louis William of Baden-Baden built a great Baroque palace there, and it remained the margraves' residence until 1771.

rif-war.s: The Rif War was fought from 1921 to 1926 between Spain, joined by France in 1925, and the Berber tribes of the Rif mountains in northern Morocco, led by Abd el-Krim, who founded the Republic of the Rif. The Spanish disaster at Annual in July 1921 cost thousands of lives and…

rio-negro.s: The Rio Negro is the largest left-bank tributary of the Amazon and the largest blackwater river in the world, rising in Colombia and flowing through Venezuela and Brazil. It joins the Amazon near Manaus, where its dark waters run beside the muddy Solimões for several kilometres.

rong-people.s: The Rong were peoples of the western and northern borderlands of ancient China whom the Zhou states regarded as outsiders. Living in the uplands of Shaanxi, Gansu and Shanxi, some were herders and others farmers in walled towns.

ruicheng.s: Ruicheng is a county in the far south-west of Shanxi, on the north bank of the Yellow River, in Yuncheng prefecture. It takes its name from the ancient State of Rui.

ramanetaka.s: Ramanetaka was a Merina prince and military governor from Madagascar who fled after the death of King Radama I and around 1830 seized the island of Moheli (Mwali) in the Comoros. He adopted Islam and the name Abderremane and ruled as sultan until his death in 1842, when his…

ranggawarsita.s: Ranggawarsita was a Javanese court poet of the Surakarta Sunanate, often called the last of the great royal poets of Java. Writing in Javanese verse, he produced historical, mystical and prophetic works, among them the Serat Kalatidha, which laments a 'time of darkness' and is…

rohtas-fort.s: Rohtas Fort is a 16th-century fortress near Jhelum in Punjab, Pakistan, built by Sher Shah Suri from about 1541 to control the Gakhar tribes and block the return of the Mughal emperor Humayun. Its walls run for about four kilometres, with massive bastions and monumental gates…

river-deveron.s: The River Deveron is a river in north-east Scotland, flowing about 100 kilometres from the hills of Aberdeenshire past Huntly and Turriff to the North Sea at Banff and Macduff. Its valley formed part of the fertile lowland of the Taexali in the Roman period.

river-don-aberdeenshire.s: The River Don is a river in north-east Scotland, flowing about 130 kilometres from the Grampian mountains through Aberdeenshire to the North Sea at Aberdeen. With the River Dee to its south, it bounded the lowlands of the Taexali in the Roman period, and the old burgh of Old…

radaa.s: Rada'a is a town in the central highlands of Yemen, in al-Bayda governorate, south-east of Sanaa. It was a home and capital of the Tahirid dynasty, which ruled much of Yemen from 1454 to 1517, and its Amiriya Madrasa, completed in 1504, is one of the most celebrated monuments…

rogun-dam.s: The Rogun Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Vakhsh river in central Tajikistan, designed to be among the tallest in the world at about 335 metres. Begun in the Soviet period in 1976, it was halted after independence; work resumed in 2016, and its first turbines began…

ritsurin-garden.s: Ritsurin Garden is a landscape garden in Takamatsu, Kagawa Prefecture, Japan, regarded as one of the finest gardens of the Edo period. Begun in the early 17th century and completed by the Matsudaira lords of Takamatsu in 1745, it combines ponds, islands, hills and pine trees…

robert-de-sable.s: Robert de Sablé was a French nobleman from Anjou and Grand Master of the Knights Templar from 1191 until his death in 1193. A commander of Richard I of England's fleet on the Third Crusade, he became master after the siege of Acre.

relaciones-geograficas.s: The Relaciones Geográficas were reports on the towns of Spain's American colonies compiled in answer to a questionnaire issued in 1577 under Philip II. Local officials described each place's history, population, resources and customs, often with maps painted by Indigenous…

ruwafa-inscriptions.s: The Ruwafa inscriptions are Greek and Nabataean Aramaic texts on a small temple at Ruwafa in the Hisma desert of north-western Saudi Arabia. Dated to 166–169 CE, they record that the temple was built by the Thamud in honour of the emperors Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus,…

rometta.s: Rometta is a hill town in the province of Messina in north-eastern Sicily. It was the last Byzantine stronghold on the island, holding out until 965, when its fall after a long siege completed the Arab conquest of Sicily begun in 827.

rule-of-the-major-generals.s: The Rule of the Major-Generals was a period of direct military government in England and Wales from August 1655 to January 1657, under Oliver Cromwell's Protectorate. After a royalist rising, the country was divided into regions, each under a major-general charged with…

ricote-valley.s: The Ricote Valley is a stretch of the Segura river valley in the Region of Murcia, south-eastern Spain, known for irrigated orchards laid out in the Islamic period. In 1228 Ibn Hud began his rising against the Almohads there.

reting-rinpoche.s: Reting Rinpoche, the fifth holder of the title, Thubten Jampal Yeshe Gyaltsen, was regent of Tibet from 1934 to 1941. He led the search that identified the Fourteenth Dalai Lama and presided over his enthronement in Lhasa in 1940.

raja-ampat-islands.s: The Raja Ampat Islands are an archipelago off the western tip of New Guinea, in Indonesia's province of Southwest Papua, centred on the islands of Waigeo, Batanta, Salawati and Misool. Their name, meaning 'four kings', recalls local rulers who owed tribute to the Sultanate of…

ros-river.s: The Ros is a river of central Ukraine, a right-bank tributary of the Dnieper about 350 kilometres long, flowing past Bila Tserkva. In the 11th and 12th centuries it formed the southern defensive line of Kievan Rus', where the princes built forts and settled Turkic allies such…

rhineland-palatinate.s: Rhineland-Palatinate is a state of western Germany, bordering France, Luxembourg and Belgium, with its capital at Mainz. It was created in 1946 in the French occupation zone from parts of the Prussian Rhine Province, the Bavarian Palatinate and Rhenish Hesse.

ravano-dalle-carceri.s: Ravano dalle Carceri was a nobleman from Verona who took part in the Fourth Crusade and became lord of the island of Euboea, or Negroponte, around 1205. He made himself a vassal of Venice in 1209, granting it trading privileges, and after his death in 1216 his lands were…

romanus-comes-africae.s: Romanus was the Roman military count (comes Africae) of the African provinces under Valentinian I. When the Austuriani raided the countryside of Leptis and Oea in the 360s, he refused to act unless the cities supplied him with provisions and thousands of camels, and later used…

ramadan-al-suwayhili.s: Ramadan al-Suwayhili was a leader of Misrata in western Libya and one of the main figures of the resistance to Italian rule. In 1915 he turned against the Italians at the battle of al-Qardabiya, a heavy defeat for their forces.

rajmala.s: The Rajmala is a chronicle of the kings of Tripura, written in Bengali verse. Its first part is traditionally dated to the 15th century, in the reign of Dharma Manikya I, and later sections continued it into the modern period.

rongelap.s: Rongelap is an atoll in the Marshall Islands, east of Bikini. Fallout from the Castle Bravo test of 1 March 1954 fell on its inhabitants, who were evacuated only two days later and suffered radiation sickness and later illnesses.

ruhnama.s: The Ruhnama, or 'Book of the Soul', is a book of spiritual and moral guidance, Turkmen history and personal reflection published under the name of Turkmenistan's president Saparmurat Niyazov, with a first volume in 2001 and a second in 2004. It became a pillar of his…

roanoke-river.s: The Roanoke River rises in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia and flows south-east into North Carolina, where it reaches Albemarle Sound. Its lower valley was home to northern Tuscarora towns, which under Tom Blount stayed out of the war of 1711.

rudamun.s: Rudamun was the last king of the Theban line known as the Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt, reigning briefly in the 8th century BCE. A younger son of Osorkon III, he succeeded his brother Takelot III.

rajpramukh.s: Rajpramukh was the title of the head of a union of former princely states in the Republic of India between 1948 and 1956, an office comparable to a state governor. Each union, such as Rajasthan, Madhya Bharat, Saurashtra or the Patiala and East Punjab States Union, had one of…

river-maigue.s: The River Maigue is a river in County Limerick, Ireland, flowing north through Croom and Adare to the Shannon estuary. In the early Middle Ages it marked the eastern edge of the lands of the Uí Fidgenti.

riyadh.s: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia, in the Najd region of central Arabia. A small oasis town, it was taken by the First Saudi State in 1773 and became the capital of the second Saudi state under Turki ibn Abdullah in 1824.

rada-of-the-belarusian-democratic-republ.n: Rada of the Belarusian Democratic Republic
rada-of-the-belarusian-democratic-republ.s: The Rada of the Belarusian Democratic Republic is the council that proclaimed Belarusian independence in Minsk on 25 March 1918, under German occupation. It issued a series of constituent charters but could not build a lasting state, and after the return of the Bolsheviks it…

rehoboam.s: Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and, according to the Hebrew Bible, the first king of Judah after the division of the united monarchy around 930 BCE. When he refused the northern tribes' demand to lighten their burdens, they made Jeroboam king, leaving Rehoboam only Judah and…

regeneration-colombia.s: The Regeneration was the political movement led by Rafael Núñez in Colombia from the 1880s that replaced the federal, liberal order of the United States of Colombia with a centralised state. Backed by Conservatives and moderate Liberals, it produced the Constitution of 1886,…

rionegro.s: Rionegro is a town in the department of Antioquia, Colombia, east of Medellín. In 1863 a convention of the victorious Liberals met there and adopted the Rionegro Constitution, which created the federal United States of Colombia, with sovereign states and broad individual…

raymond-westerling.s: Raymond Westerling was a Dutch army officer, born in Istanbul, who led counter-insurgency operations in South Sulawesi in 1946–1947 that killed thousands of Indonesians. After leaving the army he formed the Legion of Ratu Adil (APRA) and in January 1950 led an attempted coup…

river-barrow.s: The River Barrow is the second-longest river in Ireland, flowing about 190 kilometres south from the Slieve Bloom Mountains through Athy, Carlow and New Ross to Waterford Harbour. With the Nore and the Suir it forms the 'Three Sisters', and its fertile valley was settled early…

river-nore.s: The River Nore is a river of south-east Ireland, about 140 km long, rising in County Tipperary and flowing through Laois and Kilkenny to join the Barrow above New Ross. With the Barrow and the Suir it forms the 'Three Sisters' river system draining into Waterford Harbour.

rudrasena-ii.s: Rudrasena II was a king of the main branch of the Vakataka dynasty in central India in the late 4th century. He married Prabhavatigupta, daughter of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II, an alliance that brought the Vakatakas into the Gupta sphere.

rouen.s: Rouen is a city on the Seine in northern France, historic capital of Normandy. As Rotomagus it was the chief town of the Gallic Veliocasses and a Roman river port.

river-tay.s: The River Tay is the longest river in Scotland, about 190 km long, and the largest in the United Kingdom by volume of water. It flows from the western Highlands through Loch Tay and past Perth to the Firth of Tay at Dundee.

royal-botanical-expedition-to-new-granad.n: Royal Botanical Expedition to New Granada
royal-botanical-expedition-to-new-granad.s: The Royal Botanical Expedition to New Granada was a Spanish scientific enterprise directed by the priest and naturalist José Celestino Mutis from 1783 until his death in 1808 and continued until 1816. Based first at Mariquita and then in Bogotá, it described thousands of…

revolution-nationale.s: The Révolution nationale ('National Revolution') was the official ideology of the Vichy regime in France from 1940 to 1944. Proclaimed by Marshal Philippe Pétain, it replaced the republican motto with 'Work, Family, Fatherland' and promoted authoritarian rule, Catholic and…

ramayana.s: The Ramayana is a Sanskrit epic attributed to the poet Valmiki and composed over several centuries in the late 1st millennium BCE. It tells of Rama, prince of Ayodhya in Kosala, his exile, the abduction of his wife Sita by Ravana, king of Lanka, and her rescue.

raymond-bernard-trencavel.s: Raymond Bernard Trencavel was viscount of Albi and Nîmes in Languedoc in the 11th century, whose nickname Trencavel was later adopted as the name of his dynasty. razes.s: The Razès is a historical region of Languedoc in southern France, in the upper Aude valley around Limoux, named after the old town of Rhedae. A Carolingian county, it was joined to Carcassonne and passed to the Trencavel viscounts in the 11th century, and after the Albigensian…

reccared-i.s: Reccared I was king of the Visigoths from 586 to 601, the son of Liuvigild. In 587 he converted from Arian to Catholic Christianity, and at the Third Council of Toledo in 589 the Visigothic nobility and Arian bishops followed him, ending the religious division between Goths…

recceswinth.s: Recceswinth was king of the Visigoths from 649 to 672, first as co-ruler with his father Chindasuinth and alone from 653. In 654 he issued the Liber Iudiciorum, the Visigothic Code, a single law for Goths and Hispano-Romans alike that remained influential in Spain for centuries.

roderic.s: Roderic was the last king of the Visigoths in Hispania, who seized the throne around 710 amid civil strife. In 711 he was defeated and probably killed by the mainly Berber army of Tariq ibn Ziyad near the Guadalete river, opening the Iberian peninsula to the Umayyad conquest.

ranjit-vilas-palace.s: Ranjit Vilas Palace is the palace of the former rulers of Wankaner in Gujarat, western India, built on a hilltop above the town between 1907 and 1914 for Raj Sahib Amarsinhji. Its architecture combines Indian, Mughal and European Gothic and classical elements, crowned by a…

raichur.s: Raichur is a city in north-eastern Karnataka, India, with a fort begun in the late 13th century. It gives its name to the Raichur Doab, the fertile land between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, which was fought over for centuries, first by the Chalukyas and Cholas and later…

rudradaman-i.s: Rudradaman I was a ruler of the Western Satraps in the mid-2nd century CE and a grandson of Chastana. His rock inscription at Junagadh, dated to about 150 CE, records his victories over the Satavahanas and the Yaudheyas and his repair of the Sudarshana reservoir after a storm.

rudrasimha-iii.s: Rudrasimha III was the last ruler of the Western Satraps of western India, reigning in the late 4th and early 5th centuries CE. Around 395 to 415 he was defeated by the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II, who annexed Gujarat and Malwa, ending three centuries of Saka rule in the…

rheingrafenstein.s: Rheingrafenstein is a ruined castle on a rocky crag above the Nahe River near Bad Münster am Stein-Ebernburg in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. Built in the 11th or 12th century, it was the seat of the Rhinegraves, who took their name from it, until they inherited the…

red-eyebrows.s: The Red Eyebrows were a peasant rebel movement that rose in Shandong around 18 CE against Wang Mang's Xin dynasty, its fighters painting their eyebrows red to tell friend from foe. In 25 they enthroned a Han descendant, Liu Penzi, and took and sacked Chang'an.

rustaq.s: Rustaq is a town in northern Oman on the inland side of the Hajar Mountains, dominated by a large fort. In 1624 Ibadi scholars there elected Nasir ibn Murshid as imam, founding the Ya'aruba dynasty, and the town served at several times as a seat of the imams and of the early…

rohtak.s: Rohtak is a city in the Indian state of Haryana, north-west of Delhi. Excavations at the nearby mound of Khokrakot have produced coin moulds of the Yaudheya republic, showing that the area was an important Yaudheya centre in the early centuries CE.

roman-seleucid-war.s: The Roman–Seleucid War was fought from 192 to 188 BCE between the Roman Republic, with its allies Pergamon and Rhodes, and the Seleucid king Antiochus III the Great. Antiochus landed in Greece but was defeated at Thermopylae in 191 BCE and then in Anatolia at Magnesia in 190 BCE.

revolt-of-ghent-1449-1453.s: The Revolt of Ghent was a rising of the city of Ghent against Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy, provoked by his attempts to impose a salt tax and curb the city's privileges. After several years of fighting, the Ghent militia was crushed at the Battle of Gavere on 23 July 1453.

russo-swedish-war-1590-1595.s: The Russo-Swedish War of 1590–1595 was fought between the Tsardom of Russia under Feodor I, guided by Boris Godunov, and Sweden. Russia sought to recover the towns on the Gulf of Finland lost in the Livonian War.

russo-turkish-war-1686-1700.s: The Russo-Turkish War of 1686–1700 was Russia's part in the Great Turkish War as a member of the Holy League against the Ottoman Empire. Two campaigns against the Crimean Khanate under Vasily Golitsyn in 1687 and 1689 failed, but Peter I took Azov in 1696.

russo-turkish-war-1806-1812.s: The Russo-Turkish War of 1806–1812 was fought between the Russian Empire and the Ottoman Empire, mainly in the Danubian principalities. After years of indecisive campaigning, Mikhail Kutuzov trapped the main Ottoman army near Ruse in 1811.

russo-turkish-war-1828-1829.s: The Russo-Turkish War of 1828–1829 was fought between the Russian Empire and the Ottoman Empire, provoked partly by the Greek War of Independence. Russian armies crossed the Balkan mountains and took Adrianople in August 1829, while in the Caucasus they took Kars and Erzurum.
